title.zh: 卷一百十八 列傳第五十六: 苗道潤 王福 移剌眾家奴 武仙 張甫+張進 靖安民 郭文振 胡天作 張開 燕寧
title.en: Volume 118 Biographies 56: Miao Daorun, Wang Fu, Yilazhongjianu, Wu Xian, Zhang Fuzhangjin, Jing Anmin, Guo Wenzhen, Hu Tianzuo, Zhang Kai, Yan Ning
title.raw: 卷一百十八 列傳第五十六: 苗道潤 王福 移剌眾家奴 武仙 張甫+張進 靖安民 郭文振 胡天作 張開 燕寧 Volume 118 Biographies 56: Miao Daorun, Wang Fu, Yilazhongjianu, Wu Xian, Zhang Fuzhangjin, Jing Anmin, Guo Wenzhen, Hu Tianzuo, Zhang Kai, Yan Ning

sentences.zh: 苗道潤

translations.literal: Miao Daorun
translations.idiomatic: Miao Daorun

sentences.zh: 苗道潤，貞祐初，為河北義軍隊長。

translations.literal: Miao Daorun, at the beginning of the Zhenyou era, was a captain of the Hebei volunteer army.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Daorun served in the early Zhenyou period (1213–1217) as a company commander in the Hebei volunteer forces.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，河北土人往往團結為兵，或為群盜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, the natives of Hebei often banded together as soldiers, or became bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong relocated the court to Bian (Kaifeng), local Hebei men frequently organized themselves into armed bands—some as militia, others as marauders.

sentences.zh: 道潤有勇略，敢戰鬥，能得眾心。

translations.literal: Daorun had courage and stratagem, dared to fight, and could win the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun was bold and resourceful in battle and won the loyalty of his men.

sentences.zh: 比戰有功，略定城邑，遣人詣南京求官封。

translations.literal: After successive battles with merit, he roughly pacified cities and towns, and sent men to Nanjing to request official titles and enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: After a string of victories he brought several towns under control and dispatched envoys to the Southern Capital to seek formal rank and a commission.

sentences.zh: 宰相難其事，宣宗召河南轉運使王擴問曰：「卿有智慮，為朕決道潤事。

translations.literal: The chief ministers found the matter difficult. Emperor Xuanzong summoned Wang Kuo, transport commissioner of Henan, and asked, saying, "You have wisdom and deliberation—decide the matter of Daorun for Us.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were uneasy about the request. Emperor Xuanzong summoned Wang Kuo, transport commissioner for Henan, and said, "You are thoughtful—settle the Daorun question for me.

sentences.zh: 今即以其眾使為將。

translations.literal: Now We would immediately make him a general with his own following.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to appoint him general over the force he already commands.

sentences.zh: 肯終為我盡力乎？」

translations.literal: Will he in the end exert his strength fully for Us?"
translations.idiomatic: Will he stay loyal and fight for the throne to the end?"

sentences.zh: 擴對曰：「兼制天下者，以天下為度。

translations.literal: Wang Kuo replied, saying, "One who holds sway over all under Heaven measures by all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuo answered, "Whoever would govern the realm must reckon on a realm-wide scale.

sentences.zh: 道潤得眾，有功因而封之，使自為守，羈縻使之，策之上也。

translations.literal: Daorun has won the masses and has merit; therefore enfeoff him, let him guard on his own, and keep him on a tether—this is the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun holds his troops and has earned merit—enfeoff him, let him hold his own territory, and bind him with honors. That is the best policy.

sentences.zh: 今不許，彼負其眾，何所不可為。」

translations.literal: If now you do not grant it, relying on his masses, what could he not do?"
translations.idiomatic: Refuse him, and with an army at his back there is little he could not attempt."

sentences.zh: 宣宗顧謂宰執曰：「王擴之言，實契朕心。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong turned and said to the chief ministers, "Wang Kuo's words truly accord with Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his ministers and said, "Wang Kuo speaks my mind."

sentences.zh: 於是除道潤宣武將軍、同知順天軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daorun was appointed Xuanwu General and associate commissioner of the Shuntian Army command.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun was then made Xuanwu General and deputy commissioner of the Shuntian military command.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，複以功遷懷遠大將軍、同知中山府事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, again for merit he was transferred to Huaiyuan Grand General and associate prefect of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 4 (1216) he was promoted again for merit to Huaiyuan Grand General and deputy prefect of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 再閱月，複戰有功，遷驃騎上將軍、中都路經略使、兼知中山府事。

translations.literal: After another month, again fighting with merit, he was transferred to Cavalry General-in-Chief, commissioner of the Zhongdu Circuit, and concurrently prefect of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, after further victories, he rose to Cavalry General-in-Chief, commissioner for the Zhongdu circuit, while retaining charge of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，加中都留守、兼經略使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, he was additionally made garrison commander of Zhongdu and concurrent commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was also named garrison commander of Zhongdu, retaining his commissionership.

sentences.zh: 道潤前後撫定五十餘城。

translations.literal: Before and after, Daorun pacified and settled more than fifty cities.
translations.idiomatic: In all, Daorun brought more than fifty towns back under control.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，詔道潤恢復中都，以山東兵益之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, an edict ordered Daorun to recover Zhongdu, and Shandong troops were added to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) the court ordered Daorun to retake Zhongdu and reinforced him with troops from Shandong.

sentences.zh: 道潤奏：「去年十一月，臣遣總領張子明招降蠡州獨吉七斤。

translations.literal: Daorun memorialized, saying, "Last year in the eleventh month, your servant sent chief Zhang Ziming to induce Duji Qijin of Li Prefecture to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun reported: "Last November I sent my chief officer Zhang Ziming to accept the surrender of Duji Qijin at Li Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 近日，河北東路兵馬都總管移剌鐵哥移軍蠡州，襲破子明軍，殺數百人，子明亦被創。

translations.literal: Recently, Yila Tiege, overall commander of Hebei East Route forces, moved his army to Li Prefecture, raided and broke Ziming's army, killed several hundred men, and Ziming was also wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Yila Tiege, overall commander of the Hebei Eastern Route, marched on Li, routed Zhang Ziming's force, killed hundreds of men, and wounded Ziming himself.

sentences.zh: 臣將提兵問罪，重以鐵哥自拔來歸，但備之而已。

translations.literal: Your servant was about to lead troops to demand punishment, but again Tiege came of himself to submit—only guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: I was ready to march against him, but Tiege has come back into allegiance on his own; for now I need only keep watch.

sentences.zh: 今欲複取都城，乞無罪鐵哥，直令受臣節制，庶可集事。」

translations.literal: Now wishing again to take the capital city, I beg to pardon Tiege and directly order him to accept your servant's command—then the affair may be gathered to completion."
translations.idiomatic: To retake the capital I ask that Tiege be cleared and placed directly under my command so the campaign can succeed."

sentences.zh: 宣宗以問宰相，奏曰：「道潤、鐵哥不協，不可相統屬。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong asked the chief ministers; they memorialized, saying, "Daorun and Tiege are not in harmony—they cannot be made subordinate to one another."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the chief ministers, who replied: "Daorun and Tiege are at odds; neither should command the other."

sentences.zh: 詔以完顏宇行元帥府事，督道潤複中都，和輯鐵哥軍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wanyan Yu to conduct the Marshal's Bureau affairs, supervise Daorun in recovering Zhongdu, and harmonize Tiego's army.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wanyan Yu to head the Marshal's Bureau, oversee Daorun's recovery of Zhongdu, and reconcile the two armies.

sentences.zh: 初，道潤與順天軍節度使李琛不相能，兩軍士兵因之相攻，琛遣兵攻滿城、完州，道潤軍拒戰，殺琛兄榮及弟明等。

translations.literal: Earlier, Daorun and Li Chen, military commissioner of the Shuntian Army, were incompatible; soldiers of the two armies therefore attacked one another. Chen sent troops to attack Mancheng and Wan Prefecture; Daorun's army resisted, and killed Chen's elder brother Rong and younger brother Ming and others.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun had long been at odds with Li Chen, commissioner of the Shuntian command. Their troops clashed repeatedly; Chen attacked Mancheng and Wanzhou, Daorun's forces fought back, and killed Chen's brothers Rong and Ming among others.

sentences.zh: 琛奏：「潞州提控烏林答吾典承道潤風指，日謀侵害。

translations.literal: Chen memorialized, saying, "Wulinada Wudian, defense controller of Lu Prefecture, carries out Daorun's intent and daily plots harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chen accused Wulinada Wudian, defense controller at Lu Prefecture, of acting on Daorun's orders and plotting daily against him.

sentences.zh: 山東行省數諭道潤與臣通和，竟不見從，且殺臣兄榮、弟明等，恣橫如此，將為後患。」

translations.literal: The Shandong Branch Secretariat repeatedly instructed Daorun to communicate peace with your servant, yet in the end he did not comply; moreover he killed your servant's elder brother Rong and younger brother Ming and others—so wantonly overbearing, he will become a later calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong provincial authorities repeatedly urged Daorun to make peace with me, but he refused and killed my brothers Rong and Ming. Such arrogance will breed future trouble."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「乞令河北州府官不相統攝，並聽帥府節制。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, saying, "I beg that Hebei prefectural officials not command one another, but all heed the Marshal's Bureau's control.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Hebei prefects not hold authority over one another and that all answer to the Marshal's Bureau.

sentences.zh: 仍遣官增減諸路兵力，使權均勢敵無相吞併，則百姓安農畝矣。」

translations.literal: Still send officials to increase or decrease the military strength of the various routes, so that power is equal and forces matched with no mutual swallowing—then the common people will be secure in their fields."
translations.idiomatic: Send officers to adjust troop strengths route by route so no commander can overwhelm another, and the farmers may return to their fields in peace."

sentences.zh: 道潤奏李琛以眾叛，陷滿城，攻完州。

translations.literal: Daorun memorialized that Li Chen rebelled with his masses, seized Mancheng, and attacked Wan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun in turn charged Li Chen with rebellion, the seizure of Mancheng, and attacks on Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 琛亦奏道潤叛。

translations.literal: Chen also memorialized that Daorun rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Chen likewise denounced Daorun as a rebel.

sentences.zh: 廷議以為兩人失和，故至於此，令山東行省樞密院諭琛：「行省在彼，自當俱聽節制，何待帥府。

translations.literal: Court deliberation held that the two men had lost harmony and therefore came to this, and ordered the Shandong Branch Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs to instruct Chen, saying, "The Branch Secretariat is there—you should all naturally heed its control; why wait for the Marshal's Bureau?
translations.idiomatic: The court judged that mutual hatred had brought matters to this pass and instructed Chen through the Shandong civil and military authorities: "The provincial office is on the spot—you should all obey it. Why invoke the Marshal's Bureau?

sentences.zh: 士兵本以義團結，且耕且戰。

translations.literal: Soldiers and commoners originally banded together in righteousness, farming and fighting at once.
translations.idiomatic: These militias were meant to farm and fight by voluntary association.

sentences.zh: 今乃聚之城寨，遂相併吞。

translations.literal: Now they gather in walled stockades and therefore mutually swallow one another.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they crowd into fortified camps and prey on one another.

sentences.zh: 百姓不安，皆由官長無所忌憚使之然也。

translations.literal: The common people are unsettled—all because official chiefs have nothing to fear and restrain, making it so.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffer because their commanders act without restraint.

sentences.zh: 嚴為約束，依時樹藝，無致生事。」

translations.literal: Strictly impose constraints, plant and cultivate according to season, and do not cause incidents."
translations.idiomatic: Impose strict discipline, keep to the farming season, and give no cause for unrest."

sentences.zh: 有詔道潤與移剌鐵哥合兵撫定河北，令諸道兵互相應援。

translations.literal: There was an edict that Daorun and Yila Tiege combine armies to pacify and settle Hebei, and order troops of the various routes to support one another.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Daorun and Yila Tiege to join forces to pacify Hebei and directed all regional armies to support each other.

sentences.zh: 既而道潤與賈仝、賈瑀互相攻擊，詔道潤、賈仝、王福、武仙、賈瑀分畫各路元帥府控制之，彰德衛輝招撫司隸樞密院。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Daorun and Jia Tong and Jia Yu mutually attacked; an edict divided control among Daorun, Jia Tong, Wang Fu, Wu Xian, and Jia Yu for the various routes' Marshal's Bureaus, and the Zhangde-Weihui Pacification Office was subordinated to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun then clashed with Jia Tong and Jia Yu. The court partitioned Hebei among Daorun, Jia Tong, Wang Fu, Wu Xian, and Jia Yu under separate marshal jurisdictions and placed the Zhangde-Weihui pacification office under the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 賈瑀既與道潤相攻，已而詐為約和，道潤信之，遂伏兵刺殺道潤。

translations.literal: Jia Yu, having attacked Daorun, afterward feigned making peace; Daorun believed him, and therefore ambush troops stabbed and killed Daorun.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting Daorun, Jia Yu pretended to seek peace; Daorun trusted him, and Jia Yu's men ambushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不能問，一軍彷徨所依，提控靖安民乞權隸潞州行元帥府，聽其節制。

translations.literal: The court could not pursue the matter; the whole army wandered uncertain whom to rely on. Defense controller Jing Anmin begged to be provisionally subordinated to the Lu Prefecture field Marshal's Bureau and heed its control.
translations.idiomatic: The court took no action. Daorun's army was leaderless until defense controller Jing Anmin asked to place it temporarily under the Lu Prefecture field marshal's command.

sentences.zh: 時興定二年也。

translations.literal: This was in the second year of Xingding.
translations.idiomatic: This was in Xingding 2 (1218).

sentences.zh: 右丞侯摯乞以保、蠡、完三州隸真定，而蠡州舊受移剌眾家奴節制，一旦改隸真定，恐因而交爭。

translations.literal: Right Vice Chancellor Hou Zhi begged that Baoding, Li, and Wan—the three prefectures—be subordinated to Zhending, but Li Prefecture had formerly been under Yila Zhongjianu's control; suddenly changing subordination to Zhending, he feared mutual contention would arise.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Chancellor Hou Zhi proposed attaching Baoding, Li, and Wan to Zhending, but Li had long answered to Yila Zhongjianu; a sudden transfer might provoke new fighting.

sentences.zh: 靖安民等願隸潞州，乃令河北行省審處之。

translations.literal: Jing Anmin and others wished to be subordinated to Lu Prefecture; therefore the Hebei Branch Secretariat was ordered to examine and dispose.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Anmin and his men preferred Lu Prefecture, and the Hebei provincial office was told to decide.

sentences.zh: 經略副使張柔奏：「賈瑀攻易州寨，殺刺史馬信及其裨校，奪所佩金符而去。」

translations.literal: Associate commissioner Zhang Rou memorialized, saying, "Jia Yu attacked the Yi Prefecture stockade, killed Prefect Ma Xin and his staff officers, and seized the gold tally he wore and departed."
translations.idiomatic: Associate commissioner Zhang Rou reported that Jia Yu had stormed an Yi Prefecture fort, killed prefect Ma Xin and his officers, and made off with Ma's gold tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 頃之，張柔攻賈瑀殺之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Zhang Rou attacked Jia Yu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhang Rou attacked and killed Jia Yu.

sentences.zh: 道潤既死，靖安民代領其眾，是後乃封建矣。

translations.literal: After Daorun died, Jing Anmin replaced him in leading the masses; only thereafter was enfeoffment instituted.
translations.idiomatic: After Daorun's death Jing Anmin took command of his troops; only then did the court begin enfeoffing the Hebei warlords.

sentences.zh: 初，貞祐四年，右司諫術甲直敦乞封建河朔，詔尚書省議，事寢不行。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year of Zhenyou, Right Secretariat Remonstrator Shujia Zhidun begged to enfeoff the lords of the Yellow River north, an edict ordered the Ministry of State to deliberate, and the matter was laid to rest and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As early as Zhenyou 4 (1216), remonstrator Shujia Zhidun had urged enfeoffing the warlords north of the Yellow River; the Ministry of State debated the proposal, but nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，以太原不守，河北州縣不能自立，詔百官議所以為長久之利者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding, because Taiyuan could not be held and Hebei prefectures and counties could not stand on their own, an edict ordered the hundred officials to deliberate what would be a long-term benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 3 (1219), with Taiyuan lost and Hebei prefectures unable to hold out, the emperor summoned the bureaucracy to devise a lasting policy.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨徙單鎬等十有六人以謂「制兵有三，一曰戰，二曰和，三曰守。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Expositor Tushan Hao and sixteen others stated, saying, "Controlling troops has three modes: first, battle; second, peace; third, defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin expositor Tushan Hao and sixteen colleagues argued that strategy toward the enemy armies had three modes: fight, negotiate, or hold ground.

sentences.zh: 今欲戰則兵力不足，欲和則彼不肯從，唯有守耳。

translations.literal: Now if we wish to battle, military strength is insufficient; if we wish peace, they will not comply—only defense remains.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting was beyond our strength, peace was not on offer, and only defense remained feasible.

sentences.zh: 河朔州郡既殘毀，不可一概守之，宜取願就遷徙者屯于河南、陝西，其不願者許自推其長，保聚險阻。」

translations.literal: The prefectures and commanderies of the Yellow River north are already ravaged and cannot all be defended alike; it is fitting to take those willing to relocate and settle them in Henan and Shaanxi, while those unwilling should be permitted to choose their own leaders and gather in defensible terrain."
translations.idiomatic: The north-country prefectures were too ruined to defend uniformly: relocate volunteers to Henan and Shaanxi, and let those who stayed choose local leaders to hold the high ground."

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎奧屯胡撒合三人曰：「河北于河南有輔車之勢，蒲、解於陝西有襟喉之要，盡徙其民，是撤其籓籬也。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Aotun Husah and three others said, "Hebei to Henan has the momentum of chariot and outrigger; Pu and Jie to Shaanxi have the vital throat—to move all their people is to pull up the outer fence.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Aotun Husah and three others objected: "Hebei shields Henan as an outrigger shields a chariot; Pu and Jie guard Shaanxi's throat. Evacuate everyone and you tear down your own ramparts.

sentences.zh: 宜令諸郡，選才幹眾所推服、能糾眾遷徙者，願之河南或晉安、河中及諸險隘，量給之食，授以曠土，盡力耕稼。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the various commanderies to select men of talent and ability whom the masses esteem and who can marshal the masses to migrate—those willing to Henan, or Jin'an, Hezhong, and the various defiles—measuring out food to them, granting vacant land, and exerting full strength in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Let each district choose capable men the people trust to lead willing migrants to Henan, Jin'an, Hezhong, or other strongpoints, supply rations, grant vacant land, and farm it intensively.

sentences.zh: 置僑治之官，以撫循之。

translations.literal: Establish officials for diaspora governance to comfort and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint officials for these refugee settlements to oversee them.

sentences.zh: 擇其壯者，教之戰陣。

translations.literal: Select the strong among them and teach them battle arrays.
translations.idiomatic: Train the able-bodied in warfare.

sentences.zh: 敕晉安、河中守臣檄石、嵐、汾、霍之兵，以謀恢復，莫大之便。」

translations.literal: Order the garrison commanders of Jin'an and Hezhong to issue proclamations to the troops of Shi, Lan, Fen, and Huo to plan recovery—no greater convenience."
translations.idiomatic: Order the Jin'an and Hezhong garrisons to rally troops from Shi, Lan, Fen, and Huo for reconquest—a great strategic advantage."

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書烏林答與等二十一人曰：「河朔諸州，親民掌兵之職，擇土人嘗居官、有材略者授之，急則走險，無事則耕種。」

translations.literal: Minister of War Wulinada Yu and twenty-one others said, "For the various prefectures of the Yellow River north, the duties of cherishing the people and commanding troops—select natives who have formerly held office and have talent and stratagem to grant them; in urgency they flee to defiles, in peace they farm."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wulinada Yu and twenty-one others proposed: "In each north-country prefecture appoint a local man of proven office and ability to cherish the people and command troops—fighting from the hills in crisis, farming in peace."

sentences.zh: 宣徽使移剌光祖等三人曰：「度太原之勢，雖暫失之，頃亦可複。

translations.literal: Palace Commissioner Yila Guangzu and three others said, "Considering Taiyuan's situation, though temporarily lost, shortly it may also be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Commissioner Yila Guangzu and three others held that Taiyuan, though lost for the moment, could soon be retaken.

sentences.zh: 當募土人威望服眾者，假以方面重權。

translations.literal: One should recruit natives of prestige whom the masses obey, and lend them heavy authority over a region.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit locally respected men and grant them broad military authority.

sentences.zh: 能克復一道，即以本道總管授之。

translations.literal: Whoever can recover a circuit, immediately grant him that circuit's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever recovers a whole circuit should receive its overall command.

sentences.zh: 能捍州郡，即以長佐授之。

translations.literal: Whoever can defend prefectures and commanderies, immediately grant him prefectural aide rank.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever holds a prefecture should receive the appropriate prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 必能各保一方，使百姓複業。」

translations.literal: They will surely be able each to preserve one region and make the common people resume their occupations."
translations.idiomatic: Thus each region could be secured and the people restored to their livelihoods."

sentences.zh: 提點尚食局石抹穆請以高爵募民，大概同光祖議。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Imperial Pantry Bureau Shimou Mu begged to recruit the people with high rank—broadly the same as Guangzu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Pantry supervisor Shimou Mu urged recruiting locals with high rank, much as Guangzu had advised.

sentences.zh: 宰臣欲置公府，宣宗意未決，禦史中丞完顏伯嘉曰：「宋人以虛名致李全，遂有山東實地。

translations.literal: The chief ministers wished to establish ducal offices; Emperor Xuanzong's mind was not yet decided. Censor-in-Chief Wanyan Bojia said, "The Song used empty titles to win Li Quan, and thereby obtained real territory in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers favored creating princely jurisdictions, but the emperor hesitated. Censor-in-chief Wanyan Bojia said, "The Song gave Li Quan empty honors and thereby gained real ground in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 苟能統眾守土，雖三公亦何惜焉。」

translations.literal: If they can command the masses and guard territory, even the Three Dukes—what is there to spare?"
translations.idiomatic: If a man can hold territory and command troops, what matter if we make him a duke?"

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「他日事定，公府無乃多乎。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said, "When the matter is settled another day, will not the ducal offices be too many?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "When peace returns, will we not have too many princely domains?"

sentences.zh: 伯嘉曰：「若事定，以三公就節鎮何不可者。」

translations.literal: Bojia said, "If the matter is settled, what is impossible about making a Three Duke assume a military commission?"
translations.idiomatic: Bojia replied, "Once order is restored, a duke can always be folded back into the normal command structure."

sentences.zh: 宣宗意乃決。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，封滄州經略使王福為滄海公，河間路招撫使移剌眾家奴為河間公，真定經略使武仙為恆山公，中都東路經略使張甫為高陽公，中都西路經略使靖安民為易水公，遼州從宜郭文振為晉陽公，平陽招撫使胡天作為平陽公，昭義軍節度使完顏開為上党公，山東安撫副使燕寧為東莒公。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Wang Fu, commissioner of Cangzhou, was enfeoffed as Duke of Canghai; Yila Zhongjianu, pacification commissioner of Hejian Route, as Duke of Hejian; Wu Xian, commissioner of Zhending, as Duke of Hengshan; Zhang Fu, commissioner of Zhongdu East Route, as Duke of Gaoyang; Jing Anmin, commissioner of Zhongdu West Route, as Duke of Yishui; Guo Wenzhen, acting commissioner of Liaozhou, as Duke of Jinyang; Hu Tianzuo, pacification commissioner of Pingyang, as Duke of Pingyang; Wanyan Kai, military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army, as Duke of Shangdang; Yan Ning, associate pacification commissioner of Shandong, as Duke of Dongju.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xingding 4 (1220) the court enfeoffed nine warlords: Wang Fu of Cangzhou as Duke of Canghai; Yila Zhongjianu of Hejian as Duke of Hejian; Wu Xian of Zhending as Duke of Hengshan; Zhang Fu of the Zhongdu eastern route as Duke of Gaoyang; Jing Anmin of the western route as Duke of Yishui; Guo Wenzhen of Liaozhou as Duke of Jinyang; Hu Tianzuo of Pingyang as Duke of Pingyang; Wanyan Kai of the Zhaoyi army as Duke of Shangdang; and Yan Ning of Shandong as Duke of Dongju.

sentences.zh: 九公皆兼宣撫使，階銀青榮祿大夫，賜號「宣力忠臣」，總帥本路兵馬，署置官吏，征斂賦稅，賞罰號令得以便宜行之。

translations.literal: The nine dukes all concurrently served as pacification commissioners, rank Silver-Green Glory Grandee, were granted the title "Loyal Minister Who Proclaims Strength," commanded the military forces of their routes, appointed officials, levied taxes, and rewards, punishments, and orders could be carried out as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: All nine were also named pacification commissioners, ranked as Silver-Green Glory Grandees, and honored as "Loyal Ministers Who Proclaim Strength." Each commanded his route's forces, appointed officials, collected taxes, and exercised discretionary reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 仍賜詔曰：「乃者邊防不守，河朔失寧，卿等自總戎昭，備殫忠力，若能自效，朕複何憂。

translations.literal: Still an edict was granted, saying, "Recently the border defense was not kept and the Yellow River north lost tranquility; you yourselves have taken command and displayed loyalty, exhausting loyal strength—if you can render merit on your own, what worry have We?
translations.idiomatic: An edict told them: "The frontier has collapsed and the north country is in turmoil. You have taken command and shown loyalty; if you prove yourselves, I have little left to fear.

sentences.zh: 宜膺茅土之封，複賜忠臣之號。

translations.literal: It is fitting to receive enfeoffment of feudal soil, and again be granted the title of loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: You deserve feudal rank and the title of loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 除已畫定所管州縣外，如能收得鄰近州縣者，亦聽管屬。」

translations.literal: Apart from the prefectures and counties already demarcated under your control, if you can recover neighboring prefectures and counties, you are also permitted to govern them."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the prefectures already assigned, any neighboring districts you recover may be placed under your authority as well."

sentences.zh: 王福，本河北義軍，積戰功累遷同知橫海軍節度使事、滄州經略副使。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, originally of the Hebei volunteer army, through accumulated battle merit was repeatedly transferred to associate commissioner of the Henghai Army command and associate commissioner of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu came from the Hebei volunteer forces and rose through merit to deputy commissioner of the Henghai army and associate commissioner at Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，福遣提控張聚、王進複濱、棣二州，以聚攝棣州防禦使，進攝濱州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, Fu sent defense controllers Zhang Ju and Wang Jin to recover Bin and Di—the two prefectures—making Ju acting defense commissioner of Di Prefecture and Jin acting prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) Wang Fu sent Zhang Ju and Wang Jin to retake Bin and Di prefectures, with Ju as acting Di defense commissioner and Jin as acting Bin prefect.

sentences.zh: 久之，福與聚有隙，聚以棣州附于益都張林。

translations.literal: After a long time Fu and Ju had a rift; Ju attached Di Prefecture to Zhang Lin of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Wang Fu and Zhang Ju fell out, and Ju placed Di under Zhang Lin of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 興定三年九月，福上言：「滄州東濱滄海，西連真定，北備大兵，可謂要地。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Xingding, Fu submitted, saying, "Cangzhou borders the blue sea on the east, connects to Zhending on the west, and guards against great armies on the north—it may be called a vital place.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xingding 3 (1219) Wang Fu memorialized: "Cangzhou faces the sea on the east, borders Zhending on the west, and blocks the main enemy thrust from the north—it is a critical post.

sentences.zh: 乞選重臣為經略使，得便宜從事，以鎮撫軍民。」

translations.literal: I beg to select a weighty minister as commissioner, permitted to act as convenient, to pacify and comfort troops and civilians."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a senior commissioner be appointed with discretionary authority to stabilize the army and the people."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以福初率義兵複滄州，招集殘兵，今有眾萬餘，器甲完具，自雄一方。

translations.literal: The court held that Fu at first led the volunteer army to recover Cangzhou, gathered remnant troops, and now has more than ten thousand followers, weapons and armor complete, dominating a region on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The court noted that Wang Fu had first raised volunteers to retake Cangzhou, rebuilt a force of more than ten thousand well-equipped men, and now dominated his region.

sentences.zh: 與益都張林、棣州張聚皆為鄰境。

translations.literal: He borders Zhang Lin of Yidu and Zhang Ju of Di Prefecture on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: His territory adjoined Zhang Lin of Yidu and Zhang Ju of Di.

sentences.zh: 今利津已不守，遼東道路艱阻，且其意本欲自為使，但托詞耳。

translations.literal: Now Lijin is already not held, the Liaodong road is difficult and obstructed, and moreover his intent originally was to make himself commissioner—only a pretext in words.
translations.idiomatic: Lijin had fallen, contact with Liaodong was cut, and his request was plainly a pretext: he wanted the commission for himself.

sentences.zh: 因而授之，使招集濱、棣之人，通遼東音問，今若不許，宋人或以大軍迫脅，或以官爵招之，將貽後悔。」

translations.literal: Therefore grant it, and let him gather the people of Bin and Di, communicate news with Liaodong—if now you do not permit it, the Song may either coerce with a great army or recruit with official rank, and regret will be left behind."
translations.idiomatic: Granting the post would let him rally Bin and Di and restore contact with Liaodong; refusal might drive him to the Song by force or by rank, with regrets to follow."

sentences.zh: 宣宗以為然，乃以福為本州經略使，仍令自擇副使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong held it so, and therefore made Fu commissioner of his home prefecture, still ordering him to choose his own deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and made Wang Fu commissioner of Cangzhou with authority to choose his own deputy.

sentences.zh: 會福有戰功，遷遙授同知東平府事、權元帥右都監，經略節度如故。

translations.literal: As it happened Fu had battle merit and was transferred to honorary associate prefect of Dongping Prefecture and provisional right overall supervisor of the Marshalate; his commissionership and military command remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When he earned further merit he was also given honorary deputy prefect of Dongping and provisional right overall supervisor of the Marshalate, while keeping his Cangzhou commission.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，封為滄海公，以清、滄、觀州，鹽山、無棣、樂陵、東光、甯津、吳橋、將陵、阜城、蓚縣隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Canghai, with Qing, Cang, and Guan prefectures, Yanshan, Wudi, Leling, Dongguang, Ningjin, Wuqiao, Jiangling, Fucheng, and Tiao County subordinated to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4 (1220) he was enfeoffed as Duke of Canghai with jurisdiction over Qing, Cang, and Guan prefectures and the counties Yanshan, Wudi, Leling, Dongguang, Ningjin, Wuqiao, Jiangling, Fucheng, and Tiao.

sentences.zh: 四月，紅祆賊李二太尉寇樂陵，棣州張聚來攻，福皆擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Red Turban bandit Vice-Marshal Li Er raided Leling; Zhang Ju of Di Prefecture came to attack—Fu repelled them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the Red Turban leader Vice-Marshal Li Er raided Leling and Zhang Ju of Di attacked as well; Wang Fu drove off both.

sentences.zh: 李二複寇鹽山，經略副使張文與戰，李二大敗，擒其統制二人，斬首二千級，獲馬三十匹。

translations.literal: Li Er again raided Yanshan; associate commissioner Zhang Wen fought him, and Li Er was greatly defeated—two of his commanders were captured, two thousand heads cut, thirty horses obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Li Er struck Yanshan again; associate commissioner Zhang Wen routed him, captured two of his commanders, took two thousand heads, and seized thirty horses.

sentences.zh: 七月，宋人與紅祆賊入河北，福嬰城固守。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Song men and Red Turban bandits entered Hebei; Fu closed the city and firmly defended.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Song forces and Red Turbans entered Hebei; Wang Fu shut the gates and held Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 益都張林、棣州張聚日來攻掠，滄州危蹙，福將南奔，為眾所止，遂納款于張林。

translations.literal: Zhang Lin of Yidu and Zhang Ju of Di Prefecture daily came to attack and plunder; Cangzhou was critically pressed. Fu was about to flee south but was stopped by the masses, and therefore submitted to Zhang Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin and Zhang Ju attacked daily until Cangzhou was desperate. Wang Fu prepared to flee south, his men restrained him, and he submitted to Zhang Lin.

sentences.zh: 東平元帥府請討福，乞益河南步卒七千、騎兵五百，滑、浚、衛州資助芻糧，先定賞格，以待有功。

translations.literal: The Dongping Marshal's Bureau requested to campaign against Fu, begging an increase of seven thousand Henan infantry and five hundred cavalry, Huaxian, Jun, and Weizhou to supply fodder and grain, and first fixing reward scales to await those with merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongping marshal's bureau asked to punish Wang Fu, requesting seven thousand Henan infantry, five hundred cavalry, fodder from Huaxian, Jun, and Weizhou, and preset rewards for success.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以防秋在近，河南兵不可往，東平兵少，不能獨成功，待至來年春，使東平帥府與高陽公並力討之，乃止。

translations.literal: The court held that autumn defense was near, Henan troops could not go, Dongping had few troops and could not succeed alone—wait until next spring and order the Dongping marshal's bureau and the Duke of Gaoyang to campaign together; then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: With autumn defense imminent, Henan troops could not march and Dongping was too weak to act alone; the court deferred joint action with the Duke of Gaoyang until the following spring.

sentences.zh: 移剌眾家奴

translations.literal: Yila Zhongjianu
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zhongjianu

sentences.zh: 移剌眾家奴，積戰功，累官河間路招撫使，遙授開州刺史，權元帥右都監，賜姓完顏氏。

translations.literal: Yila Zhongjianu, through accumulated battle merit, was repeatedly appointed pacification commissioner of Hejian Route, honorary prefect of Kai Prefecture, provisional right overall supervisor of the Marshalate, and granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Zhongjianu rose through repeated victories to pacification commissioner of the Hejian route, honorary prefect of Kai, provisional right overall supervisor of the Marshalate, and the imperial surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，與張甫俱封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, he and Zhang Fu were both enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4 (1220) he and Zhang Fu received enfeoffment together.

sentences.zh: 眾家奴封河間公，以獻、蠡、安、深州、河間、肅甯、安平、武強、饒陽、六家莊、郎山寨隸焉。

translations.literal: Zhongjianu was enfeoffed Duke of Hejian, with Xian, Li, An, and Shen prefectures, Hejian, Suning, Anping, Wuqiang, Raoyang, Liujiazhuang, and Langshan Stockade subordinated to him.
translations.idiomatic: He became Duke of Hejian with Xian, Li, An, and Shen prefectures, Hejian, Suning, Anping, Wuqiang, Raoyang, Liujiazhuang, and Langshan Stockade under his authority.

sentences.zh: 興定末，所部州縣皆不可守。

translations.literal: At the end of Xingding, the prefectures and counties under his command could all not be held.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Xingding era none of his prefectures could be held.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，移屯信安，本張甫境內。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang, he moved his encampment to Xin'an, originally within Zhang Fu's territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang (1222) he shifted his base to Xin'an, which lay within Zhang Fu's domain.

sentences.zh: 張甫因奏：「信安本臣北境，地當沖要，乞權改為府以重之。」

translations.literal: Zhang Fu therefore memorialized, saying, "Xin'an was originally within your servant's northern border; the ground lies at a vital crossing—I beg provisionally to change it to a prefecture to give it weight."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu then argued that Xin'an lay on his northern frontier at a strategic crossing and asked that it be temporarily elevated to a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔改信安為鎮安府。

translations.literal: An edict changed Xin'an to Zhen'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court renamed Xin'an Zhen'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，與甫合兵，複取河間府及安、蠡、獻三州，與張甫皆遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year, combining troops with Fu, he again took Hejian Prefecture and the three prefectures An, Li, and Xian; he and Zhang Fu were both transferred to Grandee of the Gold Purple Glory.
translations.idiomatic: That year he joined Zhang Fu, retook Hejian and the prefectures of An, Li, and Xian, and both men were promoted to Grandee of the Gold Purple Glory.

sentences.zh: 二年，眾家奴及張甫同保鎮安，各當一面，別遣總領提控孫汝楫、楊壽、提控袁德、李成分保外垣，遂全鎮安。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zhongjianu and Zhang Fu together defended Zhen'an, each holding one face; separately they sent overall commanders and defense controllers Sun Ruqi, Yang Shou, Yuan De, and Li Cheng to defend the outer walls, and thus Zhen'an was fully secured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhongjianu and Zhang Fu jointly held Zhen'an, each responsible for one sector, while subordinates Sun Ruqi, Yang Shou, Yuan De, and Li Cheng garrisoned the outer defenses until the city was secure.

sentences.zh: 未幾，眾家奴奏：「鎮安距迎樂堌海口二百餘裏，實遼東往來之沖。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Zhongjianu memorialized, saying, "Zhen'an is more than two hundred li from Yinglegu Haikou and is in truth the crossing of traffic to and from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he reported that Zhen'an lay over two hundred li from Yinglegu Haikou on the vital sea route to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 高陽公甫有海船在鎮安西北，可募人直抵遼東，以通中外之意。

translations.literal: The Duke of Gaoyang Fu has sea vessels northwest of Zhen'an; men may be recruited to go straight to Liaodong and communicate the intent between within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Gaoyang Zhang Fu had ships northwest of Zhen'an; volunteers could sail directly to Liaodong to restore contact with the court.

sentences.zh: 若賞不重不足以使人，今擬應募者特遷忠顯校尉，授八品職，仍賞寶泉五千貫。

translations.literal: If rewards are not heavy enough to move men, now it is proposed that those who respond be specially transferred to Loyal and Illustrious Commandant, granted eighth-rank office, and still rewarded five thousand strings of treasure cash.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that recruits be made Loyal and Illustrious Commandants with eighth-rank posts and five thousand strings of treasure cash.

sentences.zh: 如官職已至忠顯八品以上者，遷兩官、升職一等，回日再遷兩官、升職二等。」

translations.literal: If office has already reached Loyal and Illustrious eighth rank or above, transfer two ranks and promote one grade; on return transfer two more ranks and promote two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Those already at eighth rank or above would advance two ranks and one grade on departure, and two more ranks and two grades on return.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 武仙，威州人。

translations.literal: Wu Xian, a man of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian was from Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或曰嘗為道士，時人以此呼之。

translations.literal: Some say he had once been a Daoist priest, and people of the time called him by this.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had been a Daoist, and contemporaries called him "the Daoist."

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，仙率鄉兵保威州西山，附者日眾，詔仙權威州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, Xian led village troops to hold the western hills of Wei Prefecture; adherents daily increased, and an edict made Xian provisional prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 (1214) he led local militia to hold the western hills of Wei; as followers grew the court named him acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，破石海於真定，宣差招撫使惟宏請加官賞，真授威州刺史，兼真定府治中，權知真定府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, he defeated Shi Hai at Zhending; the pacification commissioner on special assignment Wei Hong requested increased rank and reward; he was truly appointed prefect of Wei and concurrently aide of Zhending Prefecture, with provisional charge of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) he defeated Shi Hai at Zhending; pacification envoy Wei Hong secured his promotion to full prefect of Wei, aide of Zhending, and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 遷洺州防禦使、兼同知真定府事，遙授河平軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defense commissioner of Ming Prefecture and associate prefect of Zhending, and honorarily military commissioner of the Heiping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He became defense commissioner of Ming and associate prefect of Zhending, with honorary command of the Heiping army.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，遷知真定府事，兼經略使，遙領中京留守，權元帥右都監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding he was transferred to prefect of Zhending and concurrent commissioner, honorarily garrison commander of Zhongjing, and provisional right overall supervisor of the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4 (1220) he was prefect and commissioner of Zhending, honorary garrison commander of Zhongjing, and provisional right marshal supervisor.

sentences.zh: 無何，封恆山公，以中山、真定府，沃、冀、威、鎮寧、平定州，抱犢寨，欒城、南宮縣隸焉。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was enfeoffed Duke of Hengshan, with Zhongshan and Zhending prefectures, Wo, Ji, Wei, Zhenning, and Pingding, Baoduzhai, and Luancheng and Nangong counties subordinated to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then enfeoffed Duke of Hengshan with Zhongshan, Zhending, Wo, Ji, Wei, Zhenning, Pingding, Baoduzhai, Luancheng, and Nangong.

sentences.zh: 同時九府，財富兵強恆山最盛。

translations.literal: At the same time among the nine ducal domains, in wealth and military strength Hengshan was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Of the nine princely domains Hengshan's wealth and forces were the greatest.

sentences.zh: 是歲，歸順於大元，副史天倪治真定。

translations.literal: That year he submitted to the Great Yuan; Vice Commissioner Shi Tianni governed Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: That year he submitted to the Mongols; Shi Tianni served as deputy administrator of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 仙兄貴為安國軍節度使，史天祥擊之，貴亦歸順於大元。

translations.literal: Xian's elder brother Gui was military commissioner of the Anguo Army; Shi Tianxiang attacked him, and Gui also submitted to the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Gui, commissioner of the Anguo army, was attacked by Shi Tianxiang and also submitted.

sentences.zh: 仙與史天倪俱治真定且六年，積不相能，懼天倪圖己，嘗欲南走。

translations.literal: Xian and Shi Tianni together governed Zhending for six years, long incompatible; fearing Tianni would plot against him, he several times wished to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian and Shi Tianni co-administered Zhending for six years in mutual distrust; fearing assassination, he several times planned to flee south.

sentences.zh: 宣宗聞之，詔樞密院牒招之，仙得牒大喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong heard of it and ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to issue a proclamation summoning him; Xian received the proclamation with great joy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong summoned him by proclamation from the Bureau of Military Affairs, to Xian's delight.

sentences.zh: 正大二年，仙賊殺史天倪，複以真定來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengda, Xian treacherously killed Shi Tianni and again came to surrender with Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 2 (1225) he murdered Shi Tianni treacherously and surrendered Zhending again to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 天元大將笑乃泬討仙，仙走。

translations.literal: Great Yuan Grand General Xiaonai Jue campaigned against Xian; Xian fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol general Xiaonai Jue attacked him and he fled.

sentences.zh: 閱月，乘夜複入真定，笑乃泬複擊之，仙乃奔汴京。

translations.literal: After a month, riding the night he again entered Zhending; Xiaonai Jue again struck him, and Xian then fled to Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he re-entered Zhending by night; Xiaonai Jue drove him out again and he fled to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 五年，召見，哀宗使樞密判官白華導其禮儀，複封為恆山公，置府衛州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to audience; Emperor Aizong had Bureau of Military Affairs judge Bai Hua guide his court etiquette, and again enfeoffed him Duke of Hengshan, establishing his office at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was received in audience; Emperor Aizong had Bai Hua instruct him in court ritual and re-enfeoffed him Duke of Hengshan with his seat at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，仙圍上黨，已而大兵至，仙遁歸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Xian besieged Shangdang; shortly thereafter great armies arrived and Xian slipped back.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he besieged Shangdang but withdrew when Mongol forces arrived.

sentences.zh: 未幾，衛州被圍，內外不通。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Weizhou was besieged and inside and outside could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Weizhou was besieged and cut off.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事合達、樞密副使蒲阿救之，徙仙兵屯胡嶺關，扼金州路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Councilor Heda and Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs Pu'a to rescue it, moving Xian's troops to garrison Huguan Pass and block the Jinzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Heda and Pu'a were ordered to relieve the city; Xian's army was shifted to Huguan Pass to block the Jinzhou route.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月，大元兵涉襄漢，合達、蒲阿駐鄧州，仙由荊子口會鄧州軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, Great Yuan troops crossed Xiang and Han; Heda and Pu'a encamped at Dengzhou, and Xian joined the Dengzhou army through Jingzikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 8 Mongol forces crossed the Xiang and Han; Heda and Pu'a camped at Dengzhou and Xian joined them through Jingzikou.

sentences.zh: 天興元年正月丁酉，合達、蒲阿敗績於三峰山，仙從四十餘騎走密縣，趨禦寨，都尉烏林答胡土不納，幾為追騎所得。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the first month of the first year of Tianxing, Heda and Pu'a were defeated at Sanfeng Mountain; Xian fled with forty-odd horsemen to Mi County, hastening to the imperial camp; Commandant Wulinada Hutubu would not admit him, and he was nearly taken by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, first month, Tianxing 1 (1232), Heda and Pu'a were crushed at Sanfeng Mountain; Xian fled with some forty horsemen toward the imperial camp but was refused by Wulinada Hutubu and nearly captured.

sentences.zh: 乃舍騎，步登嵩山絕頂清涼寺，謂登封蘭若寨招撫使霍琢僧秀曰：「我豈敢入汴京。

translations.literal: He therefore abandoned his horses, climbed on foot to the summit of Mount Song at Qingliang Temple, and said to Huo Zhuo, pacification commissioner of Dengfeng Lanruozhai, the monk Xiuyue, "How would I dare enter Bianjing?
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his horses, climbed Mount Song to Qingliang Temple, and told the monk Xiuyue at Dengfeng, "I dare not enter Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 一旦有急，縛我獻大國矣。」

translations.literal: Once there is urgency, bind me and present me to the great state.
translations.idiomatic: In a crisis they would bind me and hand me to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遂走南陽留山，收潰軍得十萬人，屯留山及威遠寨。

translations.literal: He therefore fled to Liushan at Nanyang, gathered routed troops to one hundred thousand men, and encamped at Liushan and Weiyuan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Liushan in Nanyang, rallied one hundred thousand routed troops, and encamped at Liushan and Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 立官府，聚糧食，修器仗，兵勢稍振。

translations.literal: He established officials, gathered grain, repaired weapons, and military momentum gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a government, stockpiled grain, repaired arms, and gradually restored his army's strength.

sentences.zh: 三月，汴京被圍，哀宗以仙為參知政事、樞密副使，河南行省，詔與鄧州行省思烈合兵入救。

translations.literal: In the third month Bianjing was besieged; Emperor Aizong made Xian associate administering affairs and associate commissioner of military affairs for the Henan Branch Secretariat, ordering him to join forces with Silie of the Dengzhou branch to enter and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, with Kaifeng besieged, Aizong made him associate administrator and Henan military commissioner, ordering joint relief with Silie of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，至密縣東，遇大元大將速不泬兵過之，仙即按軍眉山店，報思烈曰：「阻澗結營待仙至俱進，不然敗矣。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, reaching east of Mi County, he encountered the Great Yuan Grand General Subutai's troops passing; Xian immediately held his army at Meishan Inn and reported to Silie, saying, "Block the ravine and make camp to wait until Xian arrives and advance together—otherwise you will be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month east of Mi County he met Subutai's column; he halted at Meishan Inn and warned Silie, "Camp in the defile and wait for me—or you will be defeated.

sentences.zh: 思烈急欲至汴，不聽，行至京水，大兵乘之，不戰而潰。

translations.literal: Silie urgently wished to reach Bian and would not listen; marching to Jingshui, the great army seized the moment and he collapsed without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Silie rushed toward Kaifeng and ignored him; at Jingshui the Mongols overran him without a fight.

sentences.zh: 仙亦令其軍散走，期會留山，仙至留山，潰軍至者益眾。

translations.literal: Xian also ordered his army to scatter and flee, with a rendezvous at Liushan; when Xian reached Liushan, routed troops arriving increased.
translations.idiomatic: Xian too ordered a scatter toward Liushan; more routed troops joined him there.

sentences.zh: 哀宗罷思烈為中京留守，詔仙曰：「思烈不知兵，向使從卿阻澗之策，豈有敗哉。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong removed Silie as Zhongjing garrison commander and told Xian, "Silie did not understand warfare; had he followed your plan to block the ravine, how could there have been defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Aizong demoted Silie and told Xian, "Had Silie followed your plan to hold the defile, he would not have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 軍務一以付卿，日夕以待，戮力一心，以圖後舉。」

translations.literal: Military affairs are entirely entrusted to you; day and night We wait—exert one heart together to plan the later effort.
translations.idiomatic: All military affairs are yours; exert yourself with us for what lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣刑部主事烏古論忽魯召仙，仙不欲行，乃上疏陳利害，請緩三月，生死入援。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent Ministry of Justice clerk Wugulun Hul to summon Xian; Xian did not wish to go and therefore submitted a memorial stating advantages and harms, begging three months' delay, then entering to rescue at the risk of life and death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wugulun Hul was sent to summon him; Xian refused, memorialized on strategy, and asked three months before risking all to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，思烈至鄭州，承制授宣差總領黃摑三合五朵山一帶行元帥府事、兼行六部尚書。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Silie reached Zhengzhou, by imperial commission he appointed Huang Zha Sanhe of Wuduo Mountain on special assignment as overall commander of the field Marshal's Bureau and concurrent acting minister of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier at Zhengzhou Silie had commissioned Huang Zha Sanhe as field marshal and acting head of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 及仙還留山，惡三合權盛，改為征行元帥，屯比陽。

translations.literal: When Xian returned to Liushan he disliked Sanhe's great power and changed him to campaigning field marshal, encamped at Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian returned to Liushan he demoted Sanhe to campaigning marshal at Biyang.

sentences.zh: 三合怨仙奪其權，乃歸順於大元，大將速不泬署三合守裕州。

translations.literal: Sanhe resented Xian for seizing his authority and therefore submitted to the Great Yuan; Grand General Subutai appointed Sanhe to guard Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe, resenting the loss of power, defected to the Mongols; Subutai made him guard Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三合乃詐以書約仙取裕州，可以得志。

translations.literal: Sanhe then falsely wrote in a letter agreeing with Xian to take Yuzhou so that he might achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe wrote falsely offering joint capture of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仙信之。

translations.literal: Xian believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian believed him.

sentences.zh: 三合乃報大元大將，遣兵夾擊，敗仙于柳河，仙跳走聖朵寨。

translations.literal: Sanhe then reported to the Great Yuan general and sent troops to strike from both sides, defeating Xian at Liuhe; Xian leaped and fled to Shengduo Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe informed the Mongols and attacked from two sides; Xian was beaten at Liuhe and fled to Shengduo Stockade.

sentences.zh: 初，沈丘尉曹政承制召兵西山，裕州防禦使李天祥不用命，政斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shenqiu Assistant Magistrate Cao Zheng by imperial commission raised troops in the western hills; Yuzhou Defense Commissioner Li Tianxiang did not obey orders, and Zheng executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cao Zheng of Shenqiu had raised western-hill troops; when Li Tianxiang of Yuzhou disobeyed, Zheng executed him.

sentences.zh: 仙至聖朵，謂政曰：「何故擅誅吾將？」

translations.literal: When Xian reached Shengduo he said to Zheng, "Why did you presumptuously execute my general?
translations.idiomatic: At Shengduo Xian demanded, "Why did you kill my officer without authority?

sentences.zh: 政曰：「天祥違詔，逗遛不行，政用便宜斬之。」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Tianxiang disobeyed the edict and delayed without marching—I used discretionary power to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng replied, "Tianxiang defied orders and stalled—I killed him under emergency authority.

sentences.zh: 仙怒曰：「今日宣差來起軍，明日宣差來起軍，因此軍卒戰亡殆盡矣。

translations.literal: Xian angrily said, "Today a special commissioner comes to raise the army, tomorrow a special commissioner comes to raise the army—because of this the soldiers have fought and died nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Xian raged, "Special commissioners come one day after another until the army is nearly gone.

sentences.zh: 自今選甚人來亦不聽，且教兒郎輩山中休息。」

translations.literal: From now on, no matter who is chosen to come, I will not listen, and will let the lads rest in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I heed no more envoys and let the men rest in the hills.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「天祥果有罪，待我來處置，汝何人，輒敢殺之！」

translations.literal: He also said, "If Tianxiang truly had guilt, wait for me to deal with it—what sort of person are you to dare kill him!
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If Tianxiang was guilty I would judge him—who are you to kill him!

sentences.zh: 政曰：「參政柳河失利，不知存亡，天祥違詔，何為不殺？」

translations.literal: Zheng said, "The associate administrator was defeated at Liuhe and his survival is unknown; Tianxiang disobeyed the edict—why not kill?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng retorted, "You were beaten at Liuhe—who knows if you survive? Tianxiang disobeyed—why not kill him?

sentences.zh: 仙大怒，叱左右奪政所佩銀牌，令總領楊全械系之。

translations.literal: Xian was greatly enraged and shouted for attendants to seize the silver tally Zheng wore and ordered overall commander Yang Quan to shackle him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian seized Zheng's silver tally and ordered Yang Quan to bind him.

sentences.zh: 會赦，猶囚之，及仙敗，始得釋，與楊全俱降宋。

translations.literal: When an amnesty came he was still imprisoned; only when Xian was defeated was he released, and he and Yang Quan both surrendered to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty left him imprisoned until Xian's fall; he and Yang Quan then surrendered to the Song.

sentences.zh: 是時，哀宗走歸德，遣翰林修撰魏璠間道召仙。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Aizong had fled to Guide and sent Hanlin reviser Wei Fan by a secret route to summon Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong was at Guide and sent Wei Fan by secret path to summon Xian.

sentences.zh: 行至裕州，會仙敗于柳河，璠矯詔招集潰軍以待仙，仙疑璠圖已。

translations.literal: Reaching Yuzhou, he encountered Xian's defeat at Liuhe; Fan forged an edict to gather routed troops to await Xian, and Xian suspected Fan plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuzhou Wei Fan found Xian had been beaten at Liuhe; Fan forged an edict to rally stragglers, which Xian suspected.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，仙閱兵，選鋒尚十萬，璠曰：「主上旦夕西首望公，公不宜久留於此。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Xian reviewed troops and still had one hundred thousand elite; Fan said, "The sovereign day and night looks west for you—you should not long remain here.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, Xian still had one hundred thousand picked troops; Fan urged, "The emperor looks west for you daily—you should not linger.

sentences.zh: 仙怒，幾殺璠。

translations.literal: Xian was enraged and nearly killed Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian nearly killed him in rage.

sentences.zh: 璠及忽魯剌還歸德，仙乃奏請誅璠，哀宗不聽，以璠為歸德元帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: Fan and Hul returned to Guide; Xian memorialized requesting Fan's execution, but Emperor Aizong would not listen and made Fan staff officer of the Guide marshal's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Hul returned to Guide; Xian asked to execute Fan but Aizong made him staff officer at Guide instead.

sentences.zh: 璠字邦彥，渾源人，貞祐二年進士雲。

translations.literal: Fan, style Bangyan, was a man of Hunyuan; in the second year of Zhenyou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, style Bangyan, from Hunyuan, passed the jinshi examination in Zhenyou 2 (1214).

sentences.zh: 仙部將董祐有戰功，詔賜虎符，仙畏其逼己，久不與佩。

translations.literal: Xian's subordinate Dong You had battle merit; an edict granted a tiger tally, but Xian feared he would press upon him and long did not let him wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate Dong You earned merit and was granted a tiger tally, but Xian withheld it for fear of rivalry.

sentences.zh: 祐憾之，乃結官奴欲殺仙，猶豫未敢發。

translations.literal: You resented this and therefore joined Guannu wishing to kill Xian, yet hesitated and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: You resented this and plotted with Guannu to kill Xian but hesitated.

sentences.zh: 近侍局使完顏四和有謀敢斷，嘗徵兵鄧州，圉牧使移剌呆合有異志。

translations.literal: Palace Service Bureau commissioner Wanyan Sihe had stratagem and daring decisiveness; he had once levied troops at Dengzhou; the pasture commissioner Yila Daihe had a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Palace commissioner Wanyan Sihe was bold and decisive; when levying troops at Dengzhou he found pasture commissioner Yila Daihe disloyal.

sentences.zh: 六四和以計誅之。

translations.literal: Sihe by stratagem executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sihe killed him by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 祐使謂四和曰：「仙終不肯入援，祐等位卑，力不能誅，惟君為國家圖之。」

translations.literal: You sent someone to tell Sihe, "Xian in the end will not enter to rescue; we and others are low in rank and lack strength to kill him—only you must plot for the state.
translations.idiomatic: You told Sihe, "Xian will never relieve the capital—we are too low to kill him; you must act for the state.

sentences.zh: 四和曰：「已殺呆合，複殺武仙，他日使者來，人誰肯信。」

translations.literal: Sihe said, "Already having killed Daihe, to again kill Wu Xian—when an envoy comes another day, who will believe?
translations.idiomatic: Sihe refused: "Having killed Daihe, who would believe another killing of Wu Xian?

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 仙知祐嘗有此謀，使祐使河北，其後竟殺之。

translations.literal: Xian knew You had once had this plot and sent You as envoy to Hebei; afterward he eventually killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the plot, Xian sent You to Hebei and later had him killed.

sentences.zh: 三月，仙以聖朵軍食不足，徙軍鄧州，仰給于鄧州總帥移剌瑗。

translations.literal: In the third month, because Shengduo army provisions were insufficient, Xian moved the army to Dengzhou, relying on supplies from Dengzhou overall commander Yila Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, provisions failing at Shengduo, he moved to Dengzhou to depend on Yila Yuan.

sentences.zh: 鄧州倉廩亦乏，乃分軍新野、順陽、淅川就食民家。

translations.literal: Dengzhou granaries were also depleted, and therefore he divided the army among Xinye, Shunyang, and Xichuan to eat at civilian households.
translations.idiomatic: Dengzhou stores too were empty; he dispersed troops to forage in Xinye, Shunyang, and Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 遣講議官硃概、劉琢往襄陽，借糧于宋制置使史嵩之。

translations.literal: He sent deliberation officers Zhu Gai and Liu Zhuo to Xiangyang to borrow grain from Song Commissioner Shi Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhu Gai and Liu Zhuo to Xiangyang to borrow grain from Song commissioner Shi Songzhi.

sentences.zh: 琢、概持兩端，畏留，乃以情告史嵩之曰：「仙兵勢不復振矣。」

translations.literal: Zhuo and Gai held both ends and feared being detained, and therefore told Shi Songzhi the truth, saying, "Xian's military momentum will not revive.
translations.idiomatic: Playing both sides and fearing detention, they told Songzhi that Xian's army would not recover.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「名為借糧，實欲納款，待將軍一諾耳。」

translations.literal: They also said, "Named as borrowing grain, in truth wishing to submit—only awaiting the general's one assent.
translations.idiomatic: They added that the grain mission was really an offer to surrender pending his approval.

sentences.zh: 嵩之以為實然，遣田俊持書報仙。

translations.literal: Songzhi held it true and sent Tian Jun with a letter in reply to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi believed them and sent Tian Jun with a reply.

sentences.zh: 四月，仙遣大理少卿張伯直取糧於襄陽，屯軍小江口以待之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xian sent Junior Minister of Justice Zhang Bozhi to take grain at Xiangyang, encamping the army at Xiaojiangkou to await it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Xian sent Zhang Bozhi to Xiangyang for grain, camped at Xiaojiangkou to receive it.

sentences.zh: 嵩之聞張伯直至大喜，謂仙送款矣，發書乃謝狀也，大怒，留伯直不遣。

translations.literal: Songzhi heard Zhang Bozhi had arrived with great joy, thinking Xian was sending allegiance; opening the letter it was only a letter of thanks—he was greatly enraged and detained Bozhi without releasing him.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi rejoiced at Bozhi's arrival, expecting surrender; the letter was only thanks—he detained Bozhi in fury.

sentences.zh: 仙自順陽入鄧州，移剌瑗畏逼，以女女仙，仙不疑，納之，乃還順陽。

translations.literal: Xian entered Dengzhou from Shunyang; Yila Yuan, pressed, gave his daughter to Xian in marriage; Xian did not suspect and accepted her, then returned to Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Dengzhou from Shunyang, Xian accepted Yuan's daughter in marriage without suspicion and returned to Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 鄧州糧盡，瑗終疑仙。

translations.literal: Dengzhou grain was exhausted and Yuan in the end suspected Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Dengzhou ran out of grain Yuan still distrusted him.

sentences.zh: 五月，瑗舉城降宋。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yuan surrendered the whole city to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yuan surrendered Dengzhou to the Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩之益知仙軍虛實，使孟珙率兵五千襲仙軍于順陽。

translations.literal: Songzhi further knew the truth of Xian's army and sent Meng Gong with five thousand troops to raid Xian's army at Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Songzhi, knowing Xian's weakness, sent Meng Gong with five thousand men to attack Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，仙令士卒刈麥供軍，未至二里許，始覺，仙率帳下百餘人迎擊之，孟珙不敢前。

translations.literal: At this time Xian had ordered soldiers to reap wheat for the army; not having reached two li, he first became aware; Xian led a hundred-odd men of his personal guard to meet the attack, and Meng Gong did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's men were reaping wheat; barely two li out he noticed; with a hundred guards he charged and Meng Gong held back.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，軍士稍集，有五六百人，大敗珙軍。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter soldiers gradually gathered, five or six hundred men, and greatly defeated Gong's army.
translations.idiomatic: As five or six hundred men gathered he routed Meng Gong.

sentences.zh: 珙與數百人脫走，生擒其統制、統領數十人，獲馬千餘。

translations.literal: Gong escaped with several hundred men; they captured alive his commanders and overall leaders numbering several tens of men, and obtained more than a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Gong fled with hundreds; dozens of his officers were captured and over a thousand horses taken.

sentences.zh: 至是，概、琢妄謂將納款於嵩之之語泄矣，仙皆誅之。

translations.literal: By this time the words of Gai and Zhuo falsely saying they would submit to Songzhi were leaked; Xian executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai and Zhuo's false surrender talk leaked, Xian executed them both.

sentences.zh: 移剌瑗本名粘合，字廷玉。

translations.literal: Yila Yuan's original name was Nianhe, style Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Yuan, born Nianhe, style Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 世襲契丹猛安，累功鄧州便宜總帥。

translations.literal: Hereditarily a Khitan meng'an, through accumulated merit he became convenient overall commander of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A hereditary Khitan meng'an, he rose to convenient overall commander of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至襄陽，使更姓名，稱歸正人劉介，具將校禮謁制置使。

translations.literal: Having reached Xiangyang, he was made to change his name, calling himself the returned loyalist Liu Jie, and with full staff officer etiquette paid court to the commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang he took the name Liu Jie, "returned loyalist," and paid court to the commissioner with his staff.

sentences.zh: 瑗大悔恨，明年三月，疽發背死。

translations.literal: Yuan greatly regretted it; in the third month of the next year an abscess on his back broke and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He bitterly regretted it; the next third month he died of a back abscess.

sentences.zh: 孟珙雖敗而去，仙懼宋兵複來，七月，徙淅川之石穴。

translations.literal: Although Meng Gong was defeated and left, Xian feared Song troops would come again; in the seventh month he moved to Shixue in Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Though Meng Gong was beaten, Xian feared Song return; in the seventh month he moved to Shixue in Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 是時，哀宗在蔡州，遣近侍兀顏責仙赴難，詔曰：「朕平日未嘗負卿，國家危難至此，忍擁兵自恃，坐待滅亡邪？」

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Aizong was at Caizhou and sent close attendant Wuyan to urge Xian to go to the crisis; the edict said, "We on ordinary days have never failed you; the state in peril to this point—can you bear to hold troops and rely on yourself, sitting and awaiting destruction?
translations.idiomatic: At Caizhou Aizong sent Wuyan to urge relief: "I have never wronged you—will you hoard troops and wait for ruin?

sentences.zh: 將士聞之，相視哽咽，皆願赴難與國同生死。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers hearing this looked at one another with choked sobs; all wished to go to the crisis and share life and death with the state.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wept and vowed to share the dynasty's fate.

sentences.zh: 仙懼眾心有變，乃殺馬牛，與將士三千人歃血盟誓，不負國家，眾乃大喜。

translations.literal: Xian feared the masses' hearts would change and therefore killed cattle and horses, and with three thousand officers and soldiers swore a blood oath not to fail the state; the masses then greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mutiny he slaughtered cattle, swore a blood oath with three thousand men, and they rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 無何，仙複謂眾曰：「蔡州道梗，吾兵食少，恐不能到。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Xian again told the masses, "The Caizhou road is blocked; our army has little food—I fear we cannot arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he told them, "The road to Caizhou is blocked and food is short—we may not arrive.

sentences.zh: 且蔡不可堅守，縱到亦無益。

translations.literal: Moreover Caizhou cannot be firmly held; even if we arrive it is also without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we did, Caizhou cannot be held—it would avail nothing.

sentences.zh: 近遣人覘視宋金州，百姓據山為柵極險固，廣袤百里，積糧約三百萬石。

translations.literal: Recently men were sent to reconnoiter Song Jinzhou; the common people hold the mountains as stockades extremely defensible, a hundred li in breadth and length, with grain stored of about three million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported Song Jinzhou: mountain stockades a hundred li across with some three million shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 今與汝曹共圖之，可不勞而下，留老弱守此寨以為根本，然後選勁勇趨蔡，迎上西幸，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Now with you all together plot it—we can take it without labor, leave the old and weak to hold this stockade as the root, then select the strong and brave to hurry to Caizhou, welcome the sovereign west—it is not yet late.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed taking Jinzhou easily, leaving the weak here, then striking Caizhou to escort the emperor west.

sentences.zh: 眾未及應，即令戒行李。

translations.literal: The masses had not yet responded when he immediately ordered baggage prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Before they answered he ordered baggage packed.

sentences.zh: 取淅川溯流而上，山路險阻，霖雨旬日水湍悍，老幼溺死者不可勝數，糧食絕，軍士亡者八九。

translations.literal: Taking Xichuan they went upstream; the mountain road was dangerous and obstructed, rain for ten days made the water violent and fierce, old and young drowned beyond counting, grain cut off, and soldiers lost eight or nine tenths.
translations.idiomatic: They went up the Xichuan in rain; the torrent drowned countless people; grain failed and eight or nine tenths of the army perished.

sentences.zh: 仙計無所出，八月，乃由荊子口東還，自內鄉將入聖朵寨，至峽石左右八疊秋林，聞總領楊全已降宋，留秋林十日乃遷大和。

translations.literal: Xian had no plan; in the eighth month he therefore returned east through Jingzikou, from Neixiang intending to enter Shengduo Stockade; reaching Baxie and Qiulin near Xixia, he heard overall commander Yang Quan had already surrendered to the Song; he stayed at Qiulin ten days then moved to Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he turned back through Jingzikou toward Shengduo; learning Yang Quan had surrendered at Qiulin, he lingered ten days then went to Dahe.

sentences.zh: 九月，至黑穀泊，進退失據，遂謀北走，行部尚書盧芝、侍郎石玠不從。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, reaching Heigu Po, advance and retreat lost footing, and he therefore plotted to flee north; Minister of State Lu Zhi and Vice Minister Shi Jie would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month at Heigu Po, trapped, he planned flight north; Lu Zhi and Shi Jie refused.

sentences.zh: 芝字庭瑞，河東人，任子補官，以西安軍節度使行尚書。

translations.literal: Zhi, style Tingrui, a man of Hedong, entered office by son's privilege, and as military commissioner of Xi'an Army conducted the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, style Tingrui, from Hedong, entered by yin privilege and served as acting minister as Xi'an army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 玠字子堅，河中人，崇慶二年進士，以汝州防禦使行侍郎。

translations.literal: Jie, style Zijian, a man of Hezhong, jinshi in the second year of Chongqing, and as defense commissioner of Ruzhou conducted the vice ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jie, style Zijian, from Hezhong, a Chongqing 2 jinshi, served as vice minister while defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 二人相與謀曰：「吾等知仙不恤國家久矣。

translations.literal: The two men plotted together, saying, "We know long ago that Xian does not care for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The two plotted: "We have long known Xian cares nothing for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 諫之不從，去之未可，事至今日， 正欠蔡州一死耳。

translations.literal: Remonstrance he does not follow; to leave is not yet possible—matters having come to today, we owe only one death at Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ignores advice and we cannot simply leave; at this point we owe the dynasty one death at Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 假若不得到蔡州，死於道中，猶勝死於仙也。」

translations.literal: If we still do not reach Caizhou, dying on the road is still better than dying at Xian's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Even dying on the road beats dying at Wu Xian's hands.

sentences.zh: 既去，仙始覺，追玠殺之。

translations.literal: After they had gone, Xian first became aware and pursued Jie and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Once they fled, Xian realized and killed Jie in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 芝走至南陽，為土賊所害。

translations.literal: Zhi fled to Nanyang and was killed by local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi fled to Nanyang and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 甲午，蔡州破。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Caizhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Caizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 糧且盡，將士大怨，皆散去。

translations.literal: Grain was nearly exhausted; officers and soldiers greatly resented and all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions ran out; the troops mutinied and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 仙無所歸，乃從十八人北渡河，又亡五人。

translations.literal: Xian had nowhere to return and therefore followed eighteen men north across the river, and again five perished.
translations.idiomatic: Homeless, he crossed the Yellow River north with eighteen men; five more died on the way.

sentences.zh: 五月，趨澤州，為澤之戍兵所殺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he hastened to Ze Prefecture and was killed by Ze's garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he reached Ze Prefecture and was killed by its garrison.

sentences.zh: 張甫+張進

translations.literal: Zhang Fu + Zhang Jin
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu and Zhang Jin

sentences.zh: 張甫，賜姓完顏氏。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu was granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu was granted the imperial surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 初歸順大元。

translations.literal: At first he submitted to the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He initially defected to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 涿州刺史李瘸驢招之，興定元年正月，甫與張進俱來降。

translations.literal: Zhuozhou prefect Li Bo'lv recruited him; in the first month of the first year of Xingding, Fu and Zhang Jin both came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuozhou Prefect Li Bo'lv won them over; in the first month of Xingding 1, Fu and Zhang Jin both defected.

sentences.zh: 東平行省蒙古綱承制除甫中都路經略使，進經略副使。

translations.literal: The Eastern Branch Secretariat Mongke Gang, acting under imperial commission, appointed Fu pacification commissioner of the Zhongdu Circuit and Jin deputy pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on imperial authority, Mongke Gang of the Eastern Secretariat made Fu Zhongdu Circuit pacification commissioner and Jin his deputy.

sentences.zh: 二年，苗道潤死，河北行省侯摯承制以李瘸驢權道潤中都路經略使，甫與張柔為副。

translations.literal: In the second year Miao Daorun died; Hebei Branch Secretariat Hou Zhi, acting under commission, made Li Bo'lv acting pacification commissioner of Daorun's Zhongdu Circuit, with Fu and Zhang Rou as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after Miao Daorun died, Hou Zhi of the Hebei Secretariat made Li Bo'lv acting Zhongdu Circuit pacification commissioner in Daorun's stead, with Fu and Zhang Rou as deputies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，苗道潤之眾請以靖安民代道潤。

translations.literal: Before long, Miao Daorun's followers asked that Jing Anmin replace Daorun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Daorun's troops petitioned to have Jing Anmin succeed him.

sentences.zh: 是時，張柔、安民實分掌道潤部眾，朝廷乃以瘸驢為中都東路經略使，自雄、霸以東皆隸之。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Rou and Anmin actually divided command of Daorun's forces; the court therefore made Bo'lv pacification commissioner of the Eastern Zhongdu Route, with everything from Xiong and Ba eastward subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou and Anmin now split Daorun's forces; the court made Bo'lv Eastern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner, putting Xiongzhou, Bazhou, and all points east under him.

sentences.zh: 甫、進與永定軍節度使賈仝不協，以兵相攻，奪據仝地，取仝馬以遺經略使李瘸驢，瘸驢受之。

translations.literal: Fu and Jin were at odds with Yongding Army military governor Jia Tong and attacked each other with troops, seizing Tong's territory and taking Tong's horses as a gift to pacification commissioner Li Bo'lv, who accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Jin clashed with Yongding Army governor Jia Tong, seized his territory, sent Tong's horses as tribute to Li Bo'lv, and Bo'lv accepted them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷怪瘸驢不能和輯州府，乃有向背，召瘸驢別與官職。

translations.literal: The court faulted Bo'lv for failing to harmonize prefectures and districts and for taking sides, and summoned Bo'lv to assign him another post.
translations.idiomatic: The court blamed Bo'lv for failing to keep the prefectures united and for playing favorites, and recalled him for reassignment.

sentences.zh: 召東平蒙古綱講睦甫與賈仝。

translations.literal: It summoned Mongke Gang of Dongping to mediate peace between Fu and Jia Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Mongke Gang of Dongping to reconcile Fu and Jia Tong.

sentences.zh: 綱遣同知安武軍王鬱、博野令高常住往平之，輒留瘸驢不遣，因奏曰：「張甫本受瘸驢招降，情意厚善，今遣鬱先與瘸驢議所以平之者然後可。

translations.literal: Gang sent Anwu Army vice commissioner Wang Yu and Boye magistrate Gao Chang to settle the matter, but kept Bo'lv back and would not send him, memorializing: "Zhang Fu was originally recruited and surrendered by Bo'lv, with deep goodwill between them; now if Yu is sent, he should first consult Bo'lv on how to settle matters, then proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Gang sent Wang Yu and Gao Chang to mediate but kept Bo'lv in place, explaining: "Fu originally defected at Bo'lv's invitation and they are on close terms; Wang Yu should consult Bo'lv on reconciliation first.

sentences.zh: 況甫等不識禮義之人，瘸驢就征則皆自疑，恐生他變，故不避專擅之罪。」

translations.literal: Moreover Fu and the others are men who know neither ritual nor righteousness; if Bo'lv were summoned they would all become suspicious and I fear other disturbances would arise, hence I do not shrink from the crime of usurpation."
translations.idiomatic: Fu's men are unruly; summoning Bo'lv would spook them and risk fresh trouble, so I accept the charge of overstepping my authority."

sentences.zh: 詔從綱奏。

translations.literal: The edict approved Gang's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Gang's request.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賈仝複以兵捕甫部民，殺甫參議官邢曁畢。

translations.literal: Before long Jia Tong again used troops to capture men of Fu's command and killed Fu's staff officer Xing Yibi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jia Tong raided Fu's followers and killed his aide Xing Yibi.

sentences.zh: 甫率兵攻之，賈仝敗走，遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Fu led troops to attack him; Jia Tong was defeated and fled, then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu counterattacked; Tong fled in defeat and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 甫請符印以安輯部眾，詔與之。

translations.literal: Fu requested seals and credentials to pacify and organize his command; an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu asked for official seals to rally his troops; the court granted them.

sentences.zh: 無何，李瘸驢歸順大元。

translations.literal: Before long Li Bo'lv submitted to the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Bo'lv defected to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 甫為中都東路經略使、遙授同知彰德府事、權元帥右都監。

translations.literal: Fu became Eastern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner, remotely appointed vice prefect of Zhangde Prefecture, and acting right metropolitan guard commander of the marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was made Eastern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner, given nominal vice prefect rank at Zhangde, and acting right metropolitan guard commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，張進為中都南路經略使。
