translations.literal: In the third year Zhang Jin became Southern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Zhang Jin became Southern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甫奏：「真定兵沖，乞遣重臣與恆山公武仙並力守之。」

translations.literal: Fu memorialized: "Zhending is a military hinge-point; I beg that a senior minister be sent to join forces with Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian in its defense."
translations.idiomatic: Fu urged: "Zhending is strategically vital—I beg that a senior official be sent to help Wu Xian hold it."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond.

sentences.zh: 及真定不守，甫複奏：「權元帥右都監柴茂保冀州水寨，孤立無援，若不益兵，非臣之所知也。」

translations.literal: When Zhending could no longer be held, Fu again memorialized: "Acting right metropolitan guard commander Chai Mao is holding the water fort at Jizhou, isolated without aid; if troops are not reinforced, I cannot foresee the outcome."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhending fell, Fu warned that Chai Mao's Jizhou river fort was cut off and needed reinforcements or all would be lost.

sentences.zh: 四年，甫封高陽公，以雄、莫、霸州，高陽、信安、文安、大城、保定、靜海、寶坻、武清、安次縣隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fu was enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang, with Xiong, Mo, and Ba prefectures and the counties of Gaoyang, Xin'an, Wen'an, Dacheng, Baoding, Jinghai, Baodi, Wuqing, and Anci subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Fu was created Duke of Gaoyang, receiving Xiongzhou, Mozhou, Bazhou, and nine counties.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，移剌眾家奴不能守河間，甫居之信安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang, Yelü Zhongjianu could not hold Hejian; Fu took up residence at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang, after Yelü Zhongjianu lost Hejian, Fu moved to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以功進金紫光祿大夫，始賜姓完顏。

translations.literal: That year, for merit he was promoted to Golden Purple-Robed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and was first granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: That year his merit earned him promotion to Golden Purple-Robed Grand Master and the Wanyan surname.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，張進亦遷元帥左監軍，賜姓完顏。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year Zhang Jin also was transferred to left metropolitan guard commander of the marshalate and granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two Zhang Jin became left metropolitan guard commander and received the Wanyan surname.

sentences.zh: 靖安民

translations.literal: Jing Anmin
translations.idiomatic: Jing Anmin

sentences.zh: 靖安民，德興府永興縣人。

translations.literal: Jing Anmin was a native of Yongxing County in Dexing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Anmin was from Yongxing County, Dexing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，充義軍，曆謀克、千戶、總領、萬戶、都統，皆隸苗道潤麾下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he served in the militia, passing through the ranks of company commander, chiliarch, commandant, ten-thousand-man commander, and army commander, all under Miao Daorun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he joined the militia, rising from company officer to army commander under Miao Daorun.

sentences.zh: 以功遙授定安縣令，遷涿州刺史，遙授順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: For merit he was remotely appointed magistrate of Ding'an County, transferred to Zhuozhou prefect, and remotely appointed military governor of Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: His service won him nominal magistrate rank at Ding'an, appointment as Zhuozhou prefect, and nominal Shuntian Army governorship.

sentences.zh: 充提控。

translations.literal: He served as division commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was made division commander.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，遙授安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he was remotely appointed military governor of Anwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 he received nominal Anwu Army governorship.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，遷知德興府事、中都路總領招撫使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding he was transferred to administrative commissioner of Dexing Prefecture and overall pacification commissioner of the Zhongdu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 2 he became Dexing prefectural commissioner and Zhongdu Circuit chief pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是歲，苗道潤死，安民代領其眾，行省承制以涿州刺史李瘸驢權中都路經略使。

translations.literal: That year Miao Daorun died; Anmin took command of his forces in his stead, and the branch secretariat, acting under commission, made Zhuozhou prefect Li Bo'lv acting Zhongdu Circuit pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Daorun died that year, Anmin succeeded his command; the secretariat made Li Bo'lv acting Zhongdu Circuit pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔瘸驢自雄、霸以東為中都東路經略使，自易州以西安民為中都西路經略使。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict made Bo'lv Eastern Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner from Xiong and Ba eastward, and from Yizhou westward made Anmin Western Zhongdu Route pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Bo'lv was given the east from Xiong and Ba, and Anmin the west from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 西山義軍屯壘諸招撫皆隸焉。

translations.literal: All the pacification commissioners of the Western Hills militia fortresses were subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: All Western Hills militia pacification commissioners fell under his command.

sentences.zh: 四年，遙授知德興府事，權元帥左監軍，行中都西路元帥府事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was remotely appointed administrative commissioner of Dexing Prefecture, acting left metropolitan guard commander of the marshalate, and conducted the affairs of the Western Zhongdu Route marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he received nominal Dexing prefect rank, acting left metropolitan guard command, and Western Zhongdu Route marshalate authority.

sentences.zh: 三月，安民上書曰：「苗道潤撫定州縣五十餘城，其功甚大，西京路經略使劉鐸嫉其功，反間賈瑀、李琛與道潤不協，轉相攻伐，竟以陰謀殺道潤。

translations.literal: In the third month Anmin submitted a memorial saying: "Miao Daorun pacified more than fifty prefectures and counties, a very great achievement; Western Capital Route pacification commissioner Liu Duo envied his merit, sowed discord between Jia Yu and Li Chen and Daorun so they were at odds, they successively attacked each other, and in the end Daorun was killed by intrigue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Anmin wrote: "Daorun pacified fifty-odd cities—a towering achievement. Liu Duo of the Western Capital Route envied him, turned Jia Yu and Li Chen against him, and through intrigue had him killed.

sentences.zh: 鐸令所部劉智元等掠鎮撫孫資孫、招撫楊德勝家人二十余口，錮之山寨。

translations.literal: Duo ordered his subordinates Liu Zhiyuan and others to plunder more than twenty family members of pacification commissioner Sun Zisun and recruitment commissioner Yang Desheng and confine them in a mountain fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Duo had Liu Zhiyuan seize over twenty of Sun Zisun's and Yang Desheng's relatives and lock them in a mountain fort.

sentences.zh: 若鐸常居此，恐致敗事。」

translations.literal: If Duo remains here permanently, I fear it will ruin affairs."
translations.idiomatic: If Duo stays here, disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 劉鐸亦遣副使劉璋詣南京自訴，且言：「安民侵入飛狐之境，冒濫封拜，誘惑人心，強抑總領馮通等輸銀粟。

translations.literal: Liu Duo also sent deputy commissioner Liu Zhang to the Southern Capital to plead his case, and said: "Anmin has invaded the territory of Feihu, indiscriminately granted titles, seduced men's hearts, and coerced overall commander Feng Tong and others to deliver silver and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Duo sent Liu Zhang to the Southern Capital with countercharges: Anmin had invaded Feihu, handed out bogus titles, and forced Feng Tong to supply silver and grain.

sentences.zh: 索飛狐總領王彥暉，彈壓劉智元、杜貴，欲充偏裨。

translations.literal: He demanded Feihu overall commander Wang Yanhui, suppressed Liu Zhiyuan and Du Gui, and sought to install them as staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded Wang Yanhui, bullied Liu Zhiyuan and Du Gui, and tried to make them his officers.

sentences.zh: 彥暉等拒之，輒殺貴而杖智元，竟驅彥暉而去。」

translations.literal: Yanhui and the others refused; he immediately killed Gui and flogged Zhiyuan, and in the end drove Yanhui away."
translations.idiomatic: When Yanhui refused, Anmin killed Du Gui, beat Liu Zhiyuan, and drove Yanhui out."

sentences.zh: 又言：「經略職卑，以致從宜李柏山等日謀見害。

translations.literal: He also said: "The pacification commissioner's rank is too low, so acting commissioner Li Baishan and others daily plot to harm me.
translations.idiomatic: He added that his rank was too low and Li Baishan was plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 乞許罷去。」

translations.literal: I beg to be allowed to resign."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved."

sentences.zh: 廷議，劉鐸本行招誘逋亡，今乃與安民互相論列，以起爭端。

translations.literal: At court deliberation it was held that Liu Duo had originally been tasked with recruiting fugitives, yet now he and Anmin were accusing each other back and forth, stirring up strife.
translations.idiomatic: The court found that Duo, whose mission was to win back fugitives, and Anmin were trading accusations and stoking conflict.

sentences.zh: 苗道潤死，安民實代領其眾，彥暉等軍本隸道潤，當聽安民節制。

translations.literal: Miao Daorun had died and Anmin actually commanded his forces in his stead; Yanhui's army had originally been under Daorun and should obey Anmin's command.
translations.idiomatic: Since Anmin had succeeded Daorun, Yanhui's troops, formerly Daorun's, should answer to Anmin.

sentences.zh: 乃召鐸還。

translations.literal: Duo was therefore recalled.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Duo.

sentences.zh: 頃之，封易水公，以涿、易、安肅、保州，君氏川、季鹿、三保河、北江、礬山寨、青白口、朝天寨，水谷、歡谷、車安寨隸焉。

translations.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yishui, with Zhuo, Yi, Ansu, and Bao prefectures, Junshi River, Jilu, Sanbao River, Beijiang, Fanshan Fort, Qingbaikou, Chaotian Fort, Shuigu, Huangu, and Che'an Fort subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was created Duke of Yishui, with four prefectures and a dozen fortresses under him.

sentences.zh: 十月，安民出兵至礬山，複取簷車寨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Anmin marched to Fanshan and again took Yanche Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Anmin marched to Fanshan and recaptured Yanche Fort.

sentences.zh: 大元兵圍安民所居山寨，守寨提控馬豹等以安民妻子及老弱出降，安民軍中聞之駭亂，眾議欲降以保妻子。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops besieged the mountain fortress where Anmin dwelt; fortress division commander Ma Bao and others led out Anmin's wife, children, and the aged and weak to surrender; when Anmin's army heard of it they were stricken with panic, and the multitude debated surrendering to save their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol troops besieged Anmin's fort; Ma Bao surrendered with Anmin's family and the noncombatants, and Anmin's men panicked and talked of surrender to save their families.

sentences.zh: 安民及經歷官郝端不肯從，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Anmin and his administrative officer Hao Duan refused to comply and were thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin and his aide Hao Duan refused and were killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded him Golden Purple-Robed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him Golden Purple-Robed Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 郭文振

translations.literal: Guo Wenzhen
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wenzhen

sentences.zh: 文振治遼州，深得眾心。

translations.literal: Wenzhen governed Liaozhou and deeply won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen governed Liaozhou and won deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，遷遙授中都副留守，權元帥左都監，行河東北路元帥府事，刺史、從宜如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding he was transferred to remotely appointed vice protector of the Central Capital, acting left metropolitan guard commander of the marshalate, conducting the affairs of the Eastern Hebei Route marshalate, with his posts as prefect and acting commissioner unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 3 he became nominal Central Capital vice protector, acting left metropolitan guard commander running the Eastern Hebei Route marshalate, keeping his prefect and acting commissioner posts.

sentences.zh: 文振招降太原東山二百餘村，遷老幼於山寨，得壯士七千，分駐營柵，防護秋獲。

translations.literal: Wenzhen recruited and pacified more than two hundred villages east of Taiyuan, moved the aged and young to mountain fortresses, obtained seven thousand stalwart men, and distributed them in camps and stockades to protect the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen won over two hundred villages east of Taiyuan, relocated civilians to forts, mustered seven thousand fighters, and garrisoned them to guard the harvest.

sentences.zh: 文振奏：「若秋高無兵，直取太原，河東可複。」

translations.literal: Wenzhen memorialized: "If when the autumn winds rise there are no enemy troops, we can take Taiyuan directly and recover the east of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen argued that an autumn thrust on Taiyuan could retake eastern Shanxi."

sentences.zh: 優詔許之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved.

sentences.zh: 十月，權元帥右都監、行元帥府事，與張開合堅、台州兵複取太原。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, as acting right metropolitan guard commander conducting marshalate affairs, together with Zhang Kai, He Jian, and Taizhou troops he recovered Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, as acting right guard commander, he joined Zhang Kai, He Jian, and Taizhou troops to retake Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔升樂平縣為皋州，壽陽縣西張寨為晉州，從文振之請也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict elevated Le Ping County to Gao Prefecture and Xizhang Fort of Shouyang County to Jin Prefecture, following Wenzhen's request.
translations.idiomatic: In year four, at Wenzhen's request, Le Ping County became Gao Prefecture and Xizhang Fort became Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 文振上疏曰：「揚子雲有言：'禦得其道，則天下狙詐鹹作使；

translations.literal: Wenzhen submitted a memorial saying: "Yang Ziyun said: 'If one defends in the right way, then all the cunning of the realm will serve as one's agents;
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen cited Yang Xiong: "If defense is rightly conducted, every schemer in the realm becomes your instrument;

sentences.zh: 禦失其道，則天下狙詐鹹作敵。

translations.literal: if one defends in the wrong way, then all the cunning of the realm will become one's enemies.
translations.idiomatic: if defense goes wrong, every schemer becomes your enemy.

sentences.zh: '有天下者審所禦而已。

translations.literal: One who holds the realm need only carefully consider what he is defending.
translations.idiomatic: To hold the realm, one need only choose wisely what to defend.

sentences.zh: 河朔自用兵之後，郡邑蕭然，並無官長，武夫悍卒因緣而起以為得志，僭越名位，瓜分角競，以相侵攘，雖有內除之官，亦不得領其職，所為不法，可勝言哉？

translations.literal: Since the use of troops in the North of the River, prefectures and counties lie desolate, with no magistrates at all; fierce warriors and brutal soldiers rise by opportunity thinking they have achieved their ambition, usurp ranks and titles, carve up and compete for shares, and invade and plunder one another—even where there are internally appointed officials, they cannot perform their duties; the lawless deeds, can they all be told?
translations.idiomatic: Since war came to Hebei, towns went leaderless; brutes seized power, grabbed titles, and preyed on one another while appointed officials could not govern—the abuses beggar description.

sentences.zh: 乞行帥府擅請便宜，妄自誇張以尊大其權，包藏之心蓋可知也。

translations.literal: Route marshalates on their own authority request discretionary powers, wantonly boast to aggrandize their authority—their hidden designs are surely knowable.
translations.idiomatic: Route marshalates demand discretionary powers and boast to enlarge their authority—their hidden ambitions are plain enough.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因而撫之，假權傅授，至與各路帥府力侔勢均，不相統屬。

translations.literal: The court accordingly mollified them, lent them authority and delegated power, to the point that they matched the route marshalates in strength and power and did not submit to one another's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court indulged them with borrowed authority until they rivaled official marshalates and answered to no one.

sentences.zh: 陝西行省總為節制，相去遼遠，道路梗塞，卒難聞知。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat was overall director, but the distance was vast, roads blocked, and news could scarcely reach them in time.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Secretariat nominally controlled them, but distance and blocked roads made oversight impossible.

sentences.zh: 故飛揚跋扈，無所畏憚，鄰道相望，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Therefore they were arrogant and overbearing, fearing nothing; neighboring routes looked on one another and none dared intervene.
translations.idiomatic: They grew brazen and uncontrollable; neighboring commands looked on helplessly.

sentences.zh: 自平陽城破以來，河北不置行省，朝廷信臣不復往來布揚聲教，但令曳剌行報而已。

translations.literal: Since the fall of Pingyang city, no branch secretariat had been placed in Hebei; trusted ministers of the court no longer traveled back and forth to proclaim imperial instruction, and only Ye-li messengers were sent with reports.
translations.idiomatic: Since Pingyang fell, Hebei had no branch secretariat; the court no longer sent trusted envoys, relying only on courier reports.

sentences.zh: 所司勞以酒食，悅以貨財，借其聲，共欺朝廷。

translations.literal: The responsible offices entertained them with food and wine, pleased them with goods and wealth, borrowed their reputation, and together deceived the court.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials wined, dined, and bribed them, then used their clout to deceive the court together.

sentences.zh: 奸幸既行，遂至驕恣，變故之生，何所不有，此臣所以夙夜痛心而為之憂懼也。

translations.literal: Once wicked favoritism had taken its course, they reached the point of arrogant wilfulness; what disturbance might not arise? This is why your subject is grieved day and night and filled with apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Favoritism bred arrogance and endless risk—this keeps me awake at night in dread.

sentences.zh: 乞分遣公廉之官，遍詣訪察，庶知所在利害之實。

translations.literal: I beg that upright and incorrupt officials be dispatched separately to investigate everywhere, so that the actual conditions of advantage and harm in each place may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Send honest officials to investigate everywhere and learn what truly threatens each region.

sentences.zh: 伏見澤、潞等處芻糧猶廣，人民猶眾，地多險阻，乞選重臣複置行省，皆聽節制，上下相維，可臂指使之，則國勢日重，奸惡不萌矣。」

translations.literal: I observe that at Ze and Lu and other places fodder and grain are still plentiful and the people still numerous, the terrain mostly perilous; I beg that senior ministers be selected to re-establish a branch secretariat, all obeying command, upper and lower linked together, able to be directed like arm and fingers—then the state's power would daily grow stronger and wickedness would not arise."
translations.idiomatic: Ze and Lu still have grain and people amid rugged terrain—re-establish a branch secretariat under a senior minister so upper and lower ranks move as one; national strength would grow and treachery die out."

sentences.zh: 是時，澤、潞已詔張開規劃，不能盡用文振之言，但令南京兵馬使術甲賽也行帥府于懷、孟而已。

translations.literal: At this time Ze and Lu had already been entrusted to Zhang Kai for planning; the court could not fully adopt Wenzhen's words, but only ordered Southern Capital military commissioner Shu Jiasai to conduct a marshalate at Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already assigned Zhang Kai to Ze and Lu and adopted only part of Wenzhen's plan, sending Shu Jiasai to run a marshalate at Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 是歲，封晉陽公，河東北路皆隸焉。

translations.literal: That year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinyang, and the entire Eastern Hebei Route was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was created Duke of Jinyang, with all of Eastern Hebei under him.

sentences.zh: 文振奏：「孟州每以豪猾不逞之人攝行州事，朝廷重於更代，就令主之。

translations.literal: Wenzhen memorialized: "Meng Prefecture each time has overbearing and unruly men act as provisional prefectural administrators; the court dreads replacement and lets them stay in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen reported that Mengzhou was run by thugs the court was afraid to replace.

sentences.zh: 去年，伯德和攝刺史，提控伯德安殺之，奪其職。

translations.literal: Last year Bode He acted as provisional prefect; division commander Bode An killed him and seized his post.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Bode He was acting prefect until Bode An murdered him and took over.

sentences.zh: 河東行省以陳景璠代安，安內不能平，因誣告景璠死罪，朝廷未及按問，安輒逐之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Hebei Branch Secretariat sent Chen Jingfan to replace An; An could not accept it internally and therefore falsely accused Jingfan of a capital crime; the court had not yet investigated, and An immediately drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat sent Chen Jingfan to replace An, who framed him for a capital crime and drove him out before the court could investigate.

sentences.zh: 恥受臣節制，宣言於眾，待道路稍通，當隸恆山公節制。

translations.literal: Ashamed to accept my command, he declared to the multitude that once the roads were somewhat open he would submit to the Duke of Hengshan's command.
translations.idiomatic: Refusing my authority, he announced he would transfer to Wu Xian's command when travel reopened.

sentences.zh: 今真定已不守，安猶向慕不已。

translations.literal: Now Zhending is already lost, yet An still yearns for it unceasingly.
translations.idiomatic: Even though Zhending has fallen, An still clings to Wu Xian.

sentences.zh: 臣徵兵諸郡，安輒詭辭不遣。

translations.literal: When your subject levied troops from the various prefectures, An repeatedly made excuses and would not send them.
translations.idiomatic: When I requisitioned troops, An evaded with excuses.

sentences.zh: 臣若興師，是自生一敵，非國家之便也。

translations.literal: If your subject raised an army, that would itself create an enemy—not to the state's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking him would make a new enemy—bad for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 聞安有女，臣輒違律令為侄孫述娶之，安遂見許。

translations.literal: Hearing that An had a daughter, your subject, violating statutes, had his grand-nephew Shu marry her, and An thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning An had a daughter, I broke regulations and married her to my grand-nephew Shu; An consented.

sentences.zh: 臣非願與安為姻，為公家計，屑就之耳。

translations.literal: Your subject did not wish to form a marriage alliance with An; for the public good he stooped to accept it, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: I wanted no alliance with An—I stooped to it only for the state.

sentences.zh: 自結親以來，安頗循率以從王事，法不當娶而輒娶之，敢以此罪為請。」

translations.literal: Since the marriage alliance was formed, An has fairly obeyed and followed the royal service; though the law forbade the marriage yet I rashly made it, I dare offer this as my offense."
translations.idiomatic: Since the marriage An has cooperated; I broke the law to arrange it and confess that fault."

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉其意，遣近臣慰諭之。

translations.literal: The Xuan Emperor approved his intent and sent a close minister to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan praised his loyalty and sent a courtier to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 文振複奏：「武仙所統境土甚大，雖與林州元帥府共招撫之，乞更選本土州縣官，重其職任，同與安集，可使還定。」

translations.literal: Wenzhen again memorialized: "The territory Wu Xian commands is very vast; although the Linzhou Marshalate jointly pacifies it, I beg that local prefectural and county officials be newly selected, their duties and responsibilities weighted heavily, to settle the people together, so that restoration and stability may be achieved."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen again urged that Wu Xian's vast domain needed native officials appointed with real authority to settle the region."

sentences.zh: 宣宗用其策。

translations.literal: The Xuan Emperor adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan adopted the plan.

sentences.zh: 五年，文振奏：「臣所統嵐、管、庾、石、寧化、保德諸州，境土闊遠，不能周知利害，恐誤軍國大計。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wenzhen memorialized: "The prefectures of Lan, Guan, Yu, Shi, Ninghua, and Baode under my command have vast territories; I cannot fully know their advantages and disadvantages and fear I may err in vital military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Wenzhen reported that the Lan, Guan, Yu, Shi, Ninghua, and Baode prefectures under his command sprawled too widely for him to grasp local conditions—and that mistakes there could wreck larger strategy.

sentences.zh: 伏見葭州刺史古裏甲蒲察智勇過人，深悉河東事勢，乞令行元帥府事，或為本路兵馬都總管，與臣分治。」

translations.literal: I have observed that Guliapucha, prefect of Jia Prefecture, surpasses others in wisdom and courage and understands deeply the situation in Hedong. I beg that he be ordered to conduct the affairs of the marshalate, or appointed marshal-in-chief of troops and horses on this route, to divide governance with me."
translations.idiomatic: He urged appointing Jia Prefecture's Guliapucha—bold and shrewd, deeply versed in Hedong—to run the marshalate or serve as route commander and share authority with him."

sentences.zh: 詔文振就擇可者處之便地，仍受文振節制。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wenzhen to select a suitable person and place him in a convenient location, still subject to Wenzhen's command.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Wenzhen to pick a suitable man, post him where convenient, and keep him under Wenzhen's command.

sentences.zh: 上党公張開以厚賞誘文振將士，頗有亡歸者。

translations.literal: Duke of Shangdang Zhang Kai used lavish rewards to entice Wenzhen's officers and men, and quite a few deserted to return to him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shangdang Zhang Kai lured Wenzhen's troops with rich rewards, and many deserted back to him.

sentences.zh: 詔分遼、潞粟賑太原饑民，張開不與。

translations.literal: An edict ordered grain from Liao and Lu to be divided to relieve the famine victims of Taiyuan; Zhang Kai would not supply it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered grain from Liao and Lu split to feed Taiyuan's starving people; Zhang Kai refused.

sentences.zh: 文振奏其事，詔遣使慰諭之。

translations.literal: Wenzhen memorialized the matter; an edict ordered envoys sent to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen reported this, and the court sent envoys to reassure Zhang Kai.

sentences.zh: 文振複申前請，以葭州刺史古裏甲蒲察分治嵐、管以西諸州，制可，仍令防秋後再度其宜。

translations.literal: Wenzhen again presented his earlier request, assigning Guliapucha, prefect of Jia Prefecture, to divide governance of the prefectures west of Lan and Guan. The order was approved, but he was still told to reassess the arrangement after the autumn defense season.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen renewed his request to put Guliapucha in charge west of Lan and Guan; the court agreed but told him to review the arrangement after autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 文振請分上黨粟以贍太原，詔文振與張開計度。

translations.literal: Wenzhen requested dividing Shangdang grain to provision Taiyuan; an edict ordered Wenzhen and Zhang Kai to plan together.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen asked to share Shangdang grain with Taiyuan; the court told him and Zhang Kai to work out the details.

sentences.zh: 頃之，詔以石州隸晉陽公府。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, an edict placed Shi Prefecture under the Duke of Jinyang's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Shi Prefecture was placed under the Duke of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，林州行元帥府惟良得罪召還，文振奏：「近聞惟良召還，臣竊以為不可。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang, Wei Liang of the Linzhou Marshalate was summoned back for an offense. Wenzhen memorialized: "I have recently heard that Wei Liang was summoned back; your subject privately believes this should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang (1222), Linzhou marshal Wei Liang was recalled for an offense. Wenzhen protested: "I have just heard Wei Liang is being recalled, and I do not think that wise.

sentences.zh: 惟良在林州五歲，政尚寬厚，大得民心，今茲被召，軍民遮路泣留。

translations.literal: Wei Liang had been in Linzhou for five years; his administration was generous and he won the hearts of the people greatly. Now, being summoned back, soldiers and civilians blocked the road weeping and begging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Liang had governed Linzhou five years with a generous hand and won deep loyalty; when he was recalled, soldiers and civilians blocked the road weeping and begging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 其去未幾，{山義}尖之眾作亂，逐招撫使康瑭。

translations.literal: Not long after he left, the people of Shanyijian rose in revolt and drove out pacification commissioner Kang Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he left, the people of Shanyijian rebelled and drove out pacification commissioner Kang Tang.

sentences.zh: 乞遣惟良還林州為便。」

translations.literal: I beg that Wei Liang be sent back to Linzhou—it would be best."
translations.idiomatic: Send Wei Liang back to Linzhou—that would be best."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: The request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 文振上書：「乞遣前平章政事胥鼎行省河北，諸公府、帥府並聽節制，詔諭百姓使知不忘遺黎之意，然後以河南、陝西精銳並力恢復。」

translations.literal: Wenzhen submitted a memorial: "I beg that former chief councillor Xu Ding be dispatched as branch secretariat commissioner for Hebei, with all ducal offices and marshalates under his command. Send edicts to instruct the people so they know the court has not forgotten the abandoned populace; then concentrate the elite forces of Henan and Shaanxi together to recover the lost territory."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen urged sending former chief councillor Xu Ding to Hebei as branch secretariat commissioner, putting every ducal and marshalate command under him, reassuring the people that the court had not abandoned them, then concentrating Henan and Shaanxi's best troops to recover the north."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 文振複奏：「河朔百姓引領南望，臣再四請於樞府，但以會合府兵為言。

translations.literal: Wenzhen again memorialized: "The people of Hebei crane their necks looking south; your subject has repeatedly petitioned the Military Affairs Commission, but they speak only of mustering prefectural troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen wrote again: "The people of Hebei look south in hope; I have pleaded repeatedly with the Military Affairs Commission, but they talk only of gathering local garrisons.

sentences.zh: 公府雖號分封，力實單弱，且不相統攝，所在被兵。

translations.literal: Although the ducal offices are called enfeoffments, their strength is in fact isolated and weak, and moreover they do not mutually command one another; everywhere they suffer military attack.
translations.idiomatic: The ducal fiefs look impressive on paper, but each stands alone and weak, unable to coordinate—and everywhere they are under attack.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不即遣兵複河北，人心將以為舉河朔而棄之，甚非計也。」

translations.literal: If the court does not immediately send troops to recover Hebei, people will think the entire north is being abandoned—a very poor plan indeed."
translations.idiomatic: If the court does not send troops to recover Hebei at once, people will believe all of the north has been written off—a disastrous policy."

sentences.zh: 文振大抵欲起胥鼎為行省，定河北，朝廷不能用。

translations.literal: Wenzhen's general aim was to raise Xu Ding as branch secretariat commissioner to stabilize Hebei, but the court could not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen's aim was to install Xu Ding in Hebei and restore order there, but the court would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔文振應援史詠複河東。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered Wenzhen to reinforce Shi Yong in recovering Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the court ordered Wenzhen to reinforce Shi Yong's effort to recover Hedong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，遼州不能守，徙其軍于孟州，以部將郝安等為文振副，護沿山諸寨。

translations.literal: That year, Liaozhou could not be held; its army was moved to Meng Prefecture, with subordinate generals Hao An and others as Wenzhen's deputies protecting the various mountain fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liaozhou fell; its army was moved to Meng Prefecture, with subordinates like Hao An serving as Wenzhen's deputies guarding the mountain forts.

sentences.zh: 文振辭公府，詔不許。

translations.literal: Wenzhen requested to resign his ducal office; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen tried to resign his ducal title; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 頃之，文振部將汾州招撫使王遇與孟州防禦使納蘭謀古魯不相能，複徙衛州，然亦不可以為軍，迄正大間，寓於衛而已。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, Wenzhen's subordinate Wang Yu, pacification commissioner of Fen Prefecture, and Nalan Mougulu, defense commissioner of Meng Prefecture, could not get along; they were again moved to Wei Prefecture, but it could not serve as a military base either. Through the Zhengda period they were lodged at Wei and no more.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wenzhen's subordinate Wang Yu of Fenzhou and Mengzhou's Nalan Mougulu fell out and were shifted again to Weizhou—but even there they could not sustain an army. Through the Zhengda era they merely lodged at Wei.

sentences.zh: 胡天作

translations.literal: Hu Tianzuo
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tianzuo

sentences.zh: 胡天作，字景山，管州人。

translations.literal: Hu Tianzuo, courtesy name Jingshan, was a native of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tianzuo, style name Jingshan, was from Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初以鄉兵守禦本州，累功少中大夫、管州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he defended his home prefecture with local militia; through accumulated merit he rose to vice minister of the middle rank and prefect of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: He first defended his home prefecture with local militia and, through repeated service, rose to vice minister of the middle rank and prefect of Guan.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，遙授同知太原府事，刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xingding, he was appointed by remote commission as vice administrator of Taiyuan Prefecture, retaining his prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 2 (1220) he was remotely appointed vice administrator of Taiyuan while keeping his prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 是歲，平陽失守，改同知平陽府事。

translations.literal: That year Pingyang was lost; he was changed to vice administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after Pingyang fell, he was reassigned as vice administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，複取平陽，天作言：「汾、潞皆置帥府，平陽大鎮，今稍完複，所管州縣，不下十萬戶，複業者相繼不絕，其過汾、潞遠甚，宜一體置之。」

translations.literal: In the third year, Pingyang was recovered. Tianzuo said: "Fen and Lu each have marshalates; Pingyang is a great stronghold. Now it has been somewhat restored; the prefectures and counties under its authority exceed one hundred thousand households, and those returning to their occupations come continuously without cease—far exceeding Fen and Lu. It should be treated as one whole."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Pingyang was retaken. Tianzuo argued that Fen and Lu already had marshalates, while Pingyang—a major stronghold now partly restored—governed more than one hundred thousand households with refugees returning in a steady stream, far surpassing Fen and Lu and deserving equal standing."

sentences.zh: 是時，晉安、嵐州皆有帥府，乃以天作充便宜招撫使、權元帥左都監。

translations.literal: At that time Jin'an and Lan Prefecture each had marshalates; Tianzuo was appointed provisional pacification commissioner and acting left chief overseer of the marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: Jin'an and Lan already had marshalates; Tianzuo was made provisional pacification commissioner and acting left chief overseer of the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 四年，封平陽公，以平陽、晉安府，隰、吉州隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang; Pingyang and Jin'an prefectures, and Xi and Ji prefectures, were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was created Duke of Pingyang, with Pingyang, Jin'an, Xi, and Ji placed under him.

sentences.zh: 天作請以晉安府之翼城縣為翼州，以垣曲、絳縣隸焉。

translations.literal: Tianzuo requested that Yicheng County of Jin'an Prefecture be made Yi Prefecture, with Yuanqu and Jiang Counties subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo asked that Yicheng County in Jin'an be elevated to Yi Prefecture, with Yuanqu and Jiang Counties placed under it.

sentences.zh: 置平水縣於汾河之西，朝廷皆從之。

translations.literal: He also established Pingshui County west of the Fen River; the court approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: He also created Pingshui County west of the Fen River; the court approved both requests.

sentences.zh: 初，軒成本隸程琢麾下，琢死，成率眾保隰州，以為同知隰州軍州事、兼提控軍馬。

translations.literal: At first Xuancheng had served under Cheng Zhuo; when Zhuo died, Cheng led his followers to hold Xi Prefecture and was appointed vice administrator of Xi Prefecture and concurrently chief controller of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng had first served under Cheng Zhuo; after Zhuo died he seized Xi Prefecture with his men and was made its vice administrator and chief controller of troops.

sentences.zh: 成增繕器甲，招納亡命，頗有他志。

translations.literal: Cheng added to his armor and weapons and recruited fugitives; he had ambitions beyond loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng rebuilt his arms, gathered fugitives, and showed signs of independent ambition.

sentences.zh: 是時，隰州方用兵，未可制，天作請增置要害州縣，以分其勢。

translations.literal: At that time military operations were underway at Xi Prefecture and he could not yet be restrained; Tianzuo requested adding key prefectures and counties to divide his power.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was still at war and Cheng could not yet be checked; Tianzuo asked to add strategic prefectures and counties to split his power.

sentences.zh: 隰州之境蒲縣最居其沖，可改為州，隰川之仵城鎮可改為縣，選官守備。

translations.literal: Within Xi Prefecture's borders, Pu County occupied the most critical position; it could be changed to a prefecture, and Wucheng Township of Xichuan could be changed to a county, with officials selected to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Pu County, the most exposed point in Xi Prefecture, should become a prefecture; Wucheng Township in Xichuan should become a county, each with its own garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 詔升蒲縣為蒲州，以大寧縣隸之，仵城鎮為仵城縣。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Pu County to Pu Prefecture, with Daning County subordinate to it, and Wucheng Township to Wucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted Pu County to Pu Prefecture with Daning County under it, and Wucheng Township to Wucheng County.

sentences.zh: 天作守平陽凡四年，屢有功，詔錄其子定哥為奉職。

translations.literal: Tianzuo defended Pingyang for four years in all, repeatedly achieving merit; an edict enrolled his son Dingge as an attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo held Pingyang four years with repeated success; the court enrolled his son Dingge as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 元光元年十月，青龍堡危急，詔遣古裏甲石倫會張開、郭文振兵救之，次彈平寨東三十里，不得進。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanguang, Qinglong Fort was in critical danger; an edict ordered Guliapucha Shilun to join Zhang Kai and Guo Wenzhen's troops to rescue it. They halted thirty li east of Tanping Stockade and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanguang (1222), Qinglong Fort was in grave danger; the court sent Guliapucha Shilun with Zhang Kai and Guo Wenzhen to relieve it, but they stopped thirty li east of Tanping Stockade and could not get through.

sentences.zh: 知府事術虎忽失來、總領提控王和各以兵歸順，臨城索其妻子，兵民皆潰，執天作出。

translations.literal: Prefectural administrator Tuhu Hushilai and chief controller Wang He each returned with their troops in surrender. Approaching the city they demanded their wives and children; troops and people all fled, and Tianzuo was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural administrator Tuhu Hushilai and chief controller Wang He surrendered with their troops, then marched on the city demanding their families; the garrison collapsed and Tianzuo was taken.

sentences.zh: 天作已歸順，詔誅忽失來子之南京者，命天作子定哥承應如故。

translations.literal: Tianzuo having already surrendered, an edict ordered the execution of Hushilai's son at the Southern Capital and commanded Tianzuo's son Dingge to continue his hereditary service as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianzuo surrendered, the court executed Hushilai's son in the Southern Capital and allowed Tianzuo's son Dingge to keep his hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 天作已受大元官爵，佩虎符，招撫懷、孟之民，定哥聞之，乃自經死，贈信武將軍、同知睢州軍州事。

translations.literal: Tianzuo had already accepted office and rank from the Great Yuan, wore a tiger tally, and pacified the people of Huai and Meng. When Dingge heard of this, he hanged himself. He was posthumously given the title General of Trustworthy Martiality and vice administrator of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzuo had already taken office under the Yuan, bearing a tiger tally and pacifying the people of Huai and Meng. When Dingge learned of it he hanged himself; the court posthumously made him General of Trustworthy Martiality and vice administrator of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 詔張開、郭文振招天作，天作至濟源，欲脫走，先遣人奏表南京，大元大將惡其反復，遂誅之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Kai and Guo Wenzhen to summon Tianzuo. Tianzuo reached Jiyuan and wished to escape; he first sent someone to submit a memorial at the Southern Capital. A Great Yuan general, loathing his vacillation, then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zhang Kai and Guo Wenzhen to recall Tianzuo. He reached Jiyuan planning to flee and sent a memorial to the Southern Capital first; a Yuan general, disgusted by his wavering, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 天作死後，宣宗以同知平陽府事史詠權行平陽公府事，後封平陽公。

translations.literal: After Tianzuo's death, Emperor Xuanzong had Shi Yong, vice administrator of Pingyang Prefecture, provisionally conduct the affairs of the Duke of Pingyang's office; later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianzuo's death Emperor Xuanzong put Shi Yong, vice administrator of Pingyang, in charge of the ducal office and later created him Duke of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 平陽初破，詠父祚、母蕭氏藏於窟室，索出之，使祚招詠，祚乃自縊死，蕭氏逃歸。

translations.literal: When Pingyang was first taken, Yong's father Zuo and mother Lady Xiao hid in a cave-dwelling; they were searched out. Zuo was made to summon Yong; Zuo thereupon hanged himself, and Lady Xiao escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyang first fell, Yong's father Zuo and mother Lady Xiao hid in a cave; the enemy found them and forced Zuo to summon his son. Zuo hanged himself instead, and Lady Xiao escaped home.

sentences.zh: 詠妻梗氏亦自死。

translations.literal: Yong's wife Lady Geng also killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's wife Lady Geng killed herself as well.

sentences.zh: 宣宗贈祚榮祿大夫、京兆郡公，諡成忠。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong posthumously conferred on Zuo the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Jingzhao, with the posthumous epithet Chengzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong posthumously made Zuo Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Jingzhao, with the epithet Loyal Completion.

sentences.zh: 蕭氏封京兆郡太夫人，賜號歸義。

translations.literal: Lady Xiao was enfeoffed as Grand Madame of Jingzhao Prefecture and granted the title Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiao was created Grand Madame of Jingzhao and given the title Returning to Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 梗氏贈京兆郡夫人，諡義烈。

translations.literal: Lady Geng was posthumously created Madame of Jingzhao Prefecture, with the posthumous epithet Yilie.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Geng was posthumously made Madame of Jingzhao with the epithet Righteous Fierceness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詠乞內徙，徙其軍于解州河中府。

translations.literal: Before long Yong begged to relocate inward; his army was moved to Jie Prefecture in Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yong asked to move inland; his army was transferred to Jie Prefecture in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 張開，賜姓完顏氏，景州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kai, granted the surname Wanyan, was a native of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, granted the surname Wanyan, was from Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至甯末，河北兵起，開團結鄉兵為固守，累功遙授同知清州防禦事，兼同知觀州事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhining period, when militia rose in Hebei, Kai organized local militia for defense. Through accumulated merit he was remotely appointed vice commissioner of Qing Prefecture's defense, and concurrently vice administrator of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhining (1213), as Hebei erupted in war, Kai rallied local militia for defense and, through repeated service, was remotely appointed vice commissioner of Qing Prefecture's defense and vice administrator of Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，開率所部複取河間府及滄、獻二州十有三縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, Kai led his troops to recover Hejian Prefecture and the two prefectures of Cang and Xian—thirteen counties in all.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 4 (1216) Kai retook Hejian Prefecture and thirteen counties in Cang and Xian.

sentences.zh: 開有宣撫司留付名宣敕二百道，奏乞從權署置，就任所複州縣舊官，闕者補之。

translations.literal: Kai had two hundred nominal commission edicts left with him by the pacification office; he memorialized begging permission to appoint by discretion, reinstating former prefectural and county officials at his post and filling vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Kai held two hundred blank commission edicts from the pacification office and asked to appoint officials at his discretion, restoring former prefectural and county officers and filling vacancies.

sentences.zh: 詔遷同知觀州軍州事。

translations.literal: An edict promoted him to vice administrator of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted him to vice administrator of Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開複清州，乞輸鹽易糧，詔與之糧。

translations.literal: Kai recovered Qing Prefecture and begged to trade salt for grain; an edict granted him grain.
translations.idiomatic: Kai retook Qing Prefecture and asked to exchange salt for grain; the court supplied the grain.

sentences.zh: 遷觀州刺史、權本州經略使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Guan and provisional route commissioner of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Guan and provisional route commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是，始賜姓完顏氏。

translations.literal: At this point he was first granted the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was he granted the surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 開奏乞許便宜，及論淇門、安陽、黎陽皆作堰塞水，河運不通，乞開發水道，不報。

translations.literal: Kai memorialized begging permission for discretionary authority, and argued that Qimen, Anyang, and Liyang had all built weirs to block the water so river transport was impassable; he begged to open the water route. No response.
translations.idiomatic: Kai asked for discretionary authority and reported that weirs at Qimen, Anyang, and Liyang had blocked the river route; he begged to reopen the waterway, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 觀州糧盡，是歲秋，徙軍輝州，乞麥種三千石、驢騾三百或寶券二百貫，戶部不與。

translations.literal: Guan Prefecture's grain was exhausted; that autumn the army was moved to Hui Prefecture. He begged for three thousand shi of wheat seed, three hundred donkeys and mules, or two hundred strings of treasure notes; the Revenue Bureau would not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan's grain ran out that autumn, Kai moved his army to Huizhou and asked for three thousand shi of wheat seed, three hundred pack animals, or two hundred strings of treasure notes; the Revenue Bureau refused.

sentences.zh: 禦史台奏：「開自觀州轉戰來此，久著勞績，欲令其軍耕種以自給，有司計小費拒不與。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized: "Since transferring from Guan Prefecture to fight here, Kai has long displayed labors and achievements. We wish to have his army farm for self-support, but the responsible offices, calculating petty costs, refused to grant supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported: "Kai has fought his way here from Guan with long service; we want his men to farm for themselves, but the ministries refused over petty costs.

sentences.zh: 乞斷自宸衷，與之麥種，若無牛可與，給以寶券。」

translations.literal: We beg an imperial decision to grant him wheat seed; if there are no oxen to give, grant treasure notes."
translations.idiomatic: We ask Your Majesty to decide: grant wheat seed, or treasure notes if no oxen are available."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲，潼關不守，被召入衛南京。

translations.literal: That year, Tong Pass was lost; he was summoned to guard the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after Tong Pass fell, he was recalled to defend the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，遙授澤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, he was remotely appointed prefect of Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 1 (1217) he was remotely appointed prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 二年，遙授同知彰德府、兼總領提控。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was remotely appointed vice administrator of Zhangde Prefecture and concurrently chief controller.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was remotely appointed vice administrator of Zhangde and chief controller.

sentences.zh: 三年，充潞州招撫使。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was appointed pacification commissioner of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became pacification commissioner of Lu.

sentences.zh: 林州元帥府徙潞人實林州，既複遣還。

translations.literal: The Linzhou Marshalate had moved people from Lu to populate Linzhou; once Lin was recovered they were sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The Linzhou marshalate had relocated Lu people to repopulate Linzhou; after Lin was retaken they were sent home.

sentences.zh: 開乞隸晉安元帥府，或與林州並置元帥府，各自為治。

translations.literal: Kai begged to be placed under the Jin'an Marshalate, or to have marshalates established jointly at Lin and Lu, each governing separately.
translations.idiomatic: Kai asked either to come under the Jin'an marshalate or to set up separate marshalates at Lin and Lu, each governing on its own.

sentences.zh: 十月，開以權昭義軍節度使、遙授孟州防禦使、權元帥左都監、行元帥府事，與郭文振共複太原。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Kai served as provisional military governor of the Zhaoyi Army, remotely appointed defense commissioner of Meng Prefecture, acting left chief overseer of the marshalate, and conducted the marshalate's affairs jointly with Guo Wenzhen to recover Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Kai served as provisional Zhaoyi military governor, remote Mengzhou defense commissioner, and acting left chief overseer of the marshalate, joining Guo Wenzhen to retake Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，封上黨公，以澤、潞、沁州隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang; Ze, Lu, and Qin prefectures were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was created Duke of Shangdang, with Ze, Lu, and Qin placed under him.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔複以涉縣為崇州，從開請也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict restored She County as Chong Prefecture at Kai's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court restored She County as Chong Prefecture at Kai's request.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，複取高平縣及澤州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang, Gaoping County and Ze Prefecture were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang (1222) he retook Gaoping County and Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年，大戰壺關，有功。

translations.literal: In the second year he fought a great battle at Huguan and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he fought a major battle at Huguan with distinction.

sentences.zh: 既而潞州危急，開奏：「封建公府以固屏翰，今胡天作出平陽，郭文振南徙河東，公府獨臣與史詠而已。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Prefecture was in critical danger. Kai memorialized: "Enfeoffed ducal offices were established to solidify the screen and shield of the realm. Now Hu Tianzuo holds Pingyang, Guo Wenzhen has moved south in Hedong, and of the ducal offices only your subject and Shi Yong remain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lu Prefecture was in peril. Kai wrote: "The ducal fiefs were meant to shield the realm, yet Hu Tianzuo holds Pingyang, Guo Wenzhen has shifted south in Hedong, and only Shi Yong and I remain.

sentences.zh: 乞升澤、沁二州為節鎮，以重守禦。」

translations.literal: I beg that Ze and Qin prefectures be promoted to military governorships to strengthen defense."
translations.idiomatic: Promote Ze and Qin to full military governorships to strengthen the defense."

sentences.zh: 詔以澤為忠昌軍，沁為義勝軍。

translations.literal: An edict made Ze the Zhongchang Army and Qin the Yisheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Ze the Zhongchang Army and Qin the Yisheng Army.

sentences.zh: 林州{山義}尖寨眾亂，逐招撫使康瑭，推杜仙為招撫使，開請以盧芝瑞為副，代領其眾。

translations.literal: The people of the Shanyijian stockade in Linzhou rebelled, drove out pacification commissioner Kang Tang, and installed Du Xian as pacification commissioner. Kai requested that Lu Zhirui serve as deputy to take command of the people in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyijian stockade in Linzhou rebelled, expelled Kang Tang, and made Du Xian pacification commissioner; Kai asked that Lu Zhirui serve as deputy and take command.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「比聞郭文振就食懷、孟，史詠徙解州，高倫遷葛伯寨，各自保守，民安所仰哉？

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Recently I have heard that Guo Wenzhen has gone to Huai and Meng for provisions, Shi Yong has moved to Jie Prefecture, and Gao Lun has relocated to Gebo Stockade—they each hold themselves alone. Where can the people turn for support?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I hear Guo Wenzhen has gone to Huai and Meng for supplies, Shi Yong has moved to Jie Prefecture, and Gao Lun to Gebo Stockade—each holding his own ground. What are the people to rely on?

sentences.zh: 臣領孤軍，內無儲峙，外無應援，臣不敢避失守之罪，恐益重朝廷之憂。」

translations.literal: Your subject leads an isolated army, with no stores within and no reinforcements without. Your subject does not dare shirk the fault of losing what is held, but fears only to increase the court's worries further."
translations.idiomatic: I command an isolated force with no stores within and no help without. I do not shrink from the blame if I fail—but I fear only adding to the court's burden."

sentences.zh: 正大間，潞州不守，開居南京，部曲離散，名為舊公，與匹夫無異。

translations.literal: During the Zhengda period Lu Prefecture could not be held; Kai resided at the Southern Capital. His retainers scattered; though titled a former duke, he was no different from a common man.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengda era Lu fell; Kai lived in the Southern Capital, his followers scattered, a former duke no different from any commoner.

sentences.zh: 天興初，起複，與劉益為西面元帥，領安平都尉紀綱軍五千攻衛州，敗績于白公廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, he was recalled to service. With Liu Yi he served as western route marshal, leading five thousand troops of the Jigang army of the Anping Commandant to attack Wei Prefecture; they were defeated at Baigong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianxing he was recalled and, with Liu Yi as western route marshal, led five thousand men under Anping Commandant Jigang against Weizhou; they were routed at Baigong Temple.

sentences.zh: 是時，哀宗走歸德，開與劉益謀收潰兵從衛，不果，遂與承裔西走，皆為民家所殺。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Aizong had fled to Guide; Kai and Liu Yi planned to gather scattered troops and follow at Wei but failed. They then fled west with Chengyi and were all killed by common households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong had fled to Guide; Kai and Liu Yi tried to rally broken troops at Wei but failed, then fled west with Chengyi and were killed by villagers.

sentences.zh: 初置公府，開與恆山公武仙最強。

translations.literal: When ducal offices were first established, Kai and Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian were the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: When the ducal fiefs were first created, Kai and Duke of Hengshan Wu Xian were the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 後駐兵馬武山，遣人間道請糧二萬石，用事者難之，止給二千石。

translations.literal: Later he stationed troops at Ma Wushan and sent someone by a secret route to request twenty thousand shi of grain. Those in power found it difficult and granted only two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he camped at Ma Wushan and sent a messenger by a secret route to request twenty thousand shi of grain; the court balked and sent only two thousand.

sentences.zh: 公府將佐得報皆不敢白，開聞，置酒召諸將曰：「朝廷待某特厚，今日與諸君一醉。」

translations.literal: The ducal office's assistants received the report and none dared tell him. When Kai heard, he set out wine and summoned the generals, saying, "The court treats me with especial generosity; today I shall drink one round with you all."
translations.idiomatic: His staff got the report and dared not tell him. When Kai learned of it he set out wine and called his generals: "The court has treated me with exceptional favor—today let us drink together."

sentences.zh: 諸將問故，曰：「頃以糧竭為請，祈二萬而得二千，是吾君相不以武仙輩待我也。」

translations.literal: The generals asked the reason. He said, "Just now I begged for grain because supplies were exhausted; I asked for twenty thousand and received two thousand—our ruler and ministers do not treat Wu Xian's sort and me the same way."
translations.idiomatic: When they asked why, he said, "I begged for twenty thousand shi when our grain ran out and got two thousand—the court does not treat me like Wu Xian and the others."

sentences.zh: 是時，郭文振處開西北，當兵之沖，民貧地瘠，開又不奉命以糧賑文振軍。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Wenzhen held Kai's northwest flank, facing the brunt of enemy troops; the people were poor and the land barren, and Kai also did not obey orders to provision Wenzhen's army with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wenzhen held the northwest, on the front line of enemy pressure, in a poor and barren land—and Kai also refused orders to supply Wenzhen's army with grain.

sentences.zh: 文振窮竄，開勢愈孤，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Wenzhen was driven to desperation; Kai's position grew ever more isolated, until at last he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen was driven to ruin, Kai grew ever more isolated, and in the end both were undone.

sentences.zh: 燕寧，初為莒州提控，守天勝寨，與益都田琢、東平蒙古綱相依為輔車之勢。

translations.literal: Yan Ning—at first he was division commander of Ju Prefecture, defending Tiansheng Stockade, and together with Tian Zhuo of Yidu and Menggu Gang of Dongping formed a mutual-support arrangement like paired chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ning first served as division commander of Ju Prefecture, holding Tiansheng Stockade; with Tian Zhuo of Yidu and Menggu Gang of Dongping he formed a mutual-support triangle like paired chariots.

sentences.zh: 山東雖殘破，猶倚三人為重。

translations.literal: Although Shandong was ravaged and broken, the region still relied on the three men as its pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shandong lay in ruins, the region still rested on these three men.

sentences.zh: 紅祆賊王公喜據注子堌，率眾襲據沂州。

translations.literal: The Red Turban bandit Wang Gongxi held Zhuzigu and led his followers in a surprise attack to seize Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Turban rebel Wang Gongxi held Zhuzigu and led a raid that seized Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 寧擊走之，遂複沂州，語在《田琢傳》。

translations.literal: Ning drove him off and recovered Yizhou; the account is in the biography of Tian Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Ning drove him off and retook Yizhou—the full account appears in Tian Zhuo's biography.

sentences.zh: 寧既屢破紅祆賊，招降胡七、胡八，引為腹心，賊中聞之多有欲降者。

translations.literal: After Ning repeatedly defeated the Red Turban bandits, he recruited Hu Qi and Hu Ba and brought them close as trusted confidants; many among the bandits who heard of this wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories over the Red Turbans, Ning recruited Hu Qi and Hu Ba as trusted lieutenants; many bandits hearing of this wished to surrender.

sentences.zh: 累官遙授同知安化軍節度使事、山東安撫副使。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he was remotely appointed vice commissioner of the Anhua Army and associate pacification commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Through repeated promotion he was remotely appointed vice commissioner of the Anhua Army and associate Shandong pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，封東莒公，益都府路皆隸焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongju; the entire Yidu Prefecture Route was placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 4 (1220) he was created Duke of Dongju, with the entire Yidu route placed under him.

sentences.zh: 五年，與蒙古綱、王庭玉保全東平，以功遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Menggu Gang and Wang Tingyu he preserved Dongping; for his merit he was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he preserved Dongping with Menggu Gang and Wang Tingyu and was promoted to Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 還天勝，戰死。

translations.literal: He returned to Tiansheng and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Tiansheng and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 蒙古綱奏：「寧克盡忠孝，雖位居上公，祖考未有封爵，身沒之後老稚無所衣食，乞降異恩以勵節義之士。」

translations.literal: Mongol Gang memorialized, saying, "Ning was able to exhaust loyalty and filial piety; although his rank reached the upper dukes, his ancestors and father had no enfeoffed titles—after his body perished, the old and young had nowhere to clothe and feed themselves. I beg grant a special grace to encourage men of integrity and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Mongol Gang memorialized: "Yan Ning served with perfect loyalty and filial devotion. Though he rose to princely rank, his forebears were never ennobled, and after his death his family lacked food and clothing. I ask extraordinary favors to reward such integrity."

sentences.zh: 詔贈故祖皋銀青榮祿大夫，祖母張氏范陽郡夫人，父希遷金紫光祿大夫，母彭氏、繼母許氏、妻霍氏皆為范陽郡夫人，族屬五十二人皆廩給之。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted his late grandfather Gao Silver-Green Glory Grandee, his grandmother Lady Zhang as Lady of Fanyang Commandery, his father Xi as Grandee of the Gold Purple Glory, his mother Lady Peng, stepmother Lady Xu, and wife Lady Huo all as Ladies of Fanyang Commandery, and fifty-two clansmen were all given grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously ennobled his grandfather Gao as Silver-Green Glory Grandee, his grandmother Zhang as Lady of Fanyang, his father Xi as Gold Purple Glory Grandee, his mother Peng, stepmother Xu, and wife Huo as Ladies of Fanyang, and granted stipends to fifty-two kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 自益都張林逐田涿，繼而寧死，蒙古綱勢孤，徙軍邳州，山東不復能守矣。

translations.literal: From the time Zhang Lin of Yidu drove out Tian Zhuo, and thereafter Ning died, Mongol Gang was isolated in power, moved his army to Pi Prefecture, and Shandong could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Lin of Yidu expelled Tian Zhuo and Yan Ning fell in battle, Mongol Gang stood alone, withdrew to Pi Prefecture, and Shandong was lost for good.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：苗道潤死，中分其地，靖安民有其西之半，中分以東者其後張甫有之，然無北境矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Miao Daorun died, his territory was divided in half; Jing Anmin had the western half, and the eastern half of the division Zhang Fu later held—but there was no longer a northern border.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator notes: After Miao Daorun's death his domain was split—Jing Anmin took the west, Zhang Fu later the east—but the northern frontier was gone.

sentences.zh: 大凡九公封建，《宣宗實錄》所載如此。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, the enfeoffment of the nine dukes is recorded thus in the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: In general, the enfeoffment of the nine princes is recorded thus in the Veritable Records of Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 他書載滄海公張進、河間公移剌中哥、易水公張進、晉陽公郭棟，此必正大間繼封，如史詠繼胡天作者，然不可考矣。

translations.literal: Other books record Duke of Canghai Zhang Jin, Duke of Hejian Yila Zhongge, Duke of Yishui Zhang Jin, and Duke of Jinyang Guo Dong—these must be successor enfeoffments in the Zhengda period, like Shi Yong succeeding Hu Tianzuo, yet they cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Other sources list Duke of Canghai Zhang Jin, Duke of Hejian Yila Zhongge, Duke of Yishui Zhang Jin, and Duke of Jinyang Guo Dong—likely successor titles from the Zhengda era, as Shi Yong followed Hu Tianzuo, but the details cannot be confirmed.
